1.1.m: or rather to human beings, because of [their] capacity to undertake [them],
excepting those lacking a limb, non-knowers of the Veda, eunuchs, and Śūdras;
[they belong only] to Brāhmaṇas, Kṣatriyas, and Vaiśyas, because of Vedic revelation.
A chieftain of the Niṣādas is eligible for the [sacrifice] consisting of gāvedhuka grain.
An ass-sacrifice [is prescribed] for one who has broken his vow of chastity,
The cooking of the animal cake [takes place] on the bare ground;
the cutting of the Prāśitra portion [is taken] from the penis.
In solemn rites, everything [is performed in the sacred fires], because they serve all purposes,
[There is] a prohibition of meat on what is placed upon [the fire for cooking].

1.2.m: The rest is its subsidiary rite, through textual juxtaposition and the context.
And yajati-offerings that are not endowed with fruit are its subsidiary rite.
What is the distinction between yajati-offerings and juhoti-offerings?
Oblations [poured] while standing, given with the vaṣaṭ-call, having an offering-verse and an invitatory verse, are yajati-offerings;
oblations [poured] while seated, given with the svāhā-call, are juhoti-offerings.
The officiating priests are Brāhmaṇas, because of the prohibition of consuming [the soma or oblation remnants] for the other two [classes],
In undertaking [rites] endowed with fruit, [a person acts] according to desire, because he seeks the fruit.
Not so in the case of the obligatory Agnihotra, New- and Full-Moon sacrifices, Dākṣāyaṇa, Āgrayaṇa, and animal sacrifices, because they have already been commenced.
and regarding the Four-Month sacrifices, because of the Vedic statement about the beginning of the seasons;
When [a rite is] defective, the accomplishment of the fruit [still occurs], because of the distinction between subsidiary rites and the primary rite;
and because an expiation is prescribed;
The expiation belongs to that [same] time;

1.3.m: Verses, formulas, chants, and nigadas are mantras.
Their sentence requires no further expectation [for completing its sense],
At the beginning of those [rites], the division [of mantras] is according to the purpose, because they express that [action].
The beginning of the action should coincide with the ends of the mantras, because of [their] recitation.
[The recitation of the Yajurveda is] inaudible application, because of Vedic revelation;
Upon a band with tips pointing east, one gathers the sacrificial grass with tips pointing north.
Upon [a band] with tips pointing north, [one gathers] the fuel bundle with tips pointing east.
He tucks the knots under toward the west.
The fuel bundle consists of eighteen [sticks] made of the trees [used for] enclosing sticks,
The [fuel bundle] to be brought forward is of unmeasured [sticks], with three ties.

1.3.s: nirupyājyam \\ vedo 'si \\ iti yajamāno vedaṃ karoti //
1.3.d: निरुप्याज्यम् \\ वेदो ऽसि \\ इति यजमानो वेदं करोति ॥
1.3.m: Having ladled out the clarified butter, the sacrificer makes the grass broom with [the formula], 'You are the veda.'

1.3.s: kuśamuṣṭim̐ savyāvṛttaṃ vatsajānuṃ trivṛtaṃ mūtakāryaṃ vā paśubrahmavarcasānnādyakāmā yathāsaṃkhyam //
1.3.d: कुशमुष्टिम्̐ सव्यावृत्तं वत्सजानुं त्रिवृतं मूतकार्यं वा पशुब्रह्मवर्चसान्नाद्यकामा यथासंख्यम् ॥
1.3.m: Those desiring cattle, spiritual brilliance, or proper food [make it respectively] as a handful of kuśa grass, bent to the left, [bent like] a calf's knee, threefold, or made like a woven basket, in the respective order.
[The fire is fetched] with [the words], 'From that [fire],' in the rituals; and that [applies here too].
The taking out [of the fire occurs] for each rite, when there is no continuous connection.
Once its ritual function is finished, [the fire] becomes worldly, because of its connection to the purpose.
An injunction not stated in a specific context is an isolated general statement; because it depends [on an archetype], it qualifies all [rites].
[Vessels] not connected with an oblation are made of varaṇa wood.

1.3.s: bāhumātryaḥ srucaḥ pāṇimātrapuṣkarās tvagbilā ham̐samukhaprasekā mūladaṇḍā bhavanti //
1.3.d: बाहुमात्र्यः स्रुचः पाणिमात्रपुष्करास् त्वग्बिला हम्̐समुखप्रसेका मूलदण्डा भवन्ति ॥
1.3.m: The ladles are an arm's length, with bowls measuring a palm, having their opening on the bark side, with spouts like the beak of a swan, and with handles at the base.
The dipping spoon is an aratni long, with a circular bowl [the size of] a thumb's joint.
The vessel for carrying the Prāśitra portion has the shape of a mirror,
The pathway [for movement] is between the Cātvāla pit and the rubbish heap;

1.4.m: In the absence of what is prescribed, there is no undertaking [of the rite], because that [rite] is accomplished by that [substance].
When [a rite is] obligatory, there may be a substitute on the basis of similarity.
And there would be a fault in non-completion, on account of similarity [allowing completion].
The scriptural indication has another purpose; [a substitute is not permitted] because of the injunction to take [the primary substance] again.
In the case of an observance, there is no occasion [for a substitute], because of the word of restriction.
In an optional choice, [one should continue with] that which has been begun, because [choosing another] would constitute a different rite.
When there is a conflict between the purpose and the sacrificial substance, similarity in purpose [prevails], because [the rite] is aimed at that.
Between a secondary quality and a sacrificial substance, the substance [prevails], because of its connection to the primary rite.

1.5.m: There is a sequence of actions, because they cannot occur simultaneously,
Or rather, there should be a fixed rule of sequence on the basis of explicit scripture, purpose, and textual order.
In case of conflict, the purpose [prevails], because [the rite] is aimed at that.
Explicit scripture [prevails] over textual order, because [the latter] is inferential.
Between a mantra and an injunction, the force of the mantra [prevails], because it is used directly in practice.
When equals concur, that which is common comes first, because of its connection with sequence.
Not in a single rite, because of the connection [of components].
However, in drawing, placing, cutting, and offering, [the sequence is determined] by explicit statement.
Not when the sacrificial substances are different, because of the connection of secondary qualities—so says Vātsya.
Once begun, [the primary substance] is obligatory, because of the specific fault [of abandoning it].
In the case of the Ṣoḍaśin, however, [it must be taken] because of the preponderance of sequence.
There is no fixed rule in rites associated with personal results.
Sequence is for the sake of the injunction, because [simultaneous performance] in an action is impossible.

1.6.m: When a cut-off portion is destroyed, [another cut-off portion should be taken from] another [part of the substance], so as to maintain the subsidiary features.
Because it is linked to the sequence, as in the case of the Sviṣṭakṛt offering.
When a subordinate feature fails, however, [the rite proceeds] because a remainder exists.
The deity, the fire, the sacred words, and the actions cannot [have substitutes], because they are for the sake of another.
A prohibited [item cannot be a substitute], on account of demerit.
Among subordinate factors, there is a substitute, because they serve another purpose.
He has the same ritual duties, because he engages in the action.
Sacrificial sessions belong only to Brahmins, because the scripture specifies them as the officiating priests.
[They must be] of the same ritual procedure, so that there is no defect.
A Vaiśya and a Rājanya [may perform the role] in the Gārhapatya rite.
The thousand-year [sacrificial session] is for non-humans, because it is impossible [for humans].
Because it is possible according to the scripture, says Bhāradvāja.
It is a clan sacrificial session, says Kārṣṇājini.
It concludes after half [the time], says Laugākṣi.

1.7.m: The simultaneous occurrence of actions constitutes a common procedure.
On account of capability, human purpose, being accomplished [once], having a single purpose, co-presence, and scriptural statements.
[A common procedure applies] when there is identity of result, rite, place, time, sacrificial substance, deity, and subordinate details.
In a series of days, the Subrahmaṇyā formula indicates everything, as in the archetype rite.
The rite whose time falls within the common procedure [is done once], because it is not enjoined for each individual day.
When an action is repeated over a single sacrificial substance, the recitation of the mantra occurs once, because [its purpose] is accomplished.
Not so, however, in the case of taking, reaping, spreading, and scooping clarified butter.

However, during sleep, crossing a river, rainfall, sight of an impure thing, and setting out on a journey, [the expiatory mantra is recited] once, because the time and substance have a single purpose.
The time of a secondary rite [occurs] once, because they do not coincide.
And the chip of wood, because of the instruction for the completion [of the rite].
The master [performs] the primary rite, because of his connection to the fruit.
In the mantras and consecrations connected with a person, [and] in renunciation, on account of capacity.
The others [perform] the rest, according to their designations.
In circular movements and around borders, moving clockwise.

1.7.s: viparyasya pitryeṣu tu sakṛd dakṣiṇā ca //
1.7.d: विपर्यस्य पित्र्येषु तु सकृद् दक्षिणा च ॥
1.7.m: Reversing [this] in rites for the ancestors, however, [it is done] once and toward the south.
When the primary sacrificial substance is spoiled, there is a repetition [of the primary rite] along with its subsidiaries, because it is enjoined with them.

1.8.m: When subordinate factors serve a single purpose, all are undertaken, because they are enjoined.
If it be argued that there would be purposelessness of Vedic statement,
[we reply:] its purposefulness would be at another time.
In mere ritual attributes, there is combination, because there is no contradiction,
Not [so] in the offering-verses and invocatory verses, because of contradiction,
In expiations, [there is option] because the fault is removed [by any one].
The application of accent in a mantra is as handed down in the sacred text, because there is no distinction.
Or it is the Brāhmaṇa accent, because the mantras are taught in the context [of the Brāhmaṇa].

There is monotone in sacrifice, [even] in calling from a distance, except for the Subrahmaṇyā recitation, the sāman chants, silent muttered prayers, the nyūṅkha recitation, and the sacrificer's formulas.
There is an option of numbers in connection with giving gifts, because [the giving] is accomplished [by any specified number].
In the cases of the stomach-contents, the omentum, the udder, and the rectum, there is combination, because of the consecrated nature of the substance and because of their distinctness.
And in the case of injunctions regarding subordinate details, because of the general rule and specific attachment.
One should not pass between the Gārhapatya and Āhavanīya fires.
Or turning around, turning back, or turning otherwise.
The sacrificial ritual is conducted from the north.
The seats of the Brahman priest and the sacrificer are to the south.
Behind [is] the sacrificer, touching the altar.
The Adhvaryu priest is [engaged] in the rites, because of his connection with the Veda.
Another [performs] in case of express text or contradiction.
Among the sacrificial material, the vessels, the sacrificer, and the officiating priests, each preceding one is interior [closer to the altar].
And among the officiating priests according to priority.
The yajati-offerings in the Āhavanīya fire are from the Dhruvā ladle.
And some [say] also the Iḍā portion, the Prāśitra portion, and the Āghāra libations.
Oblations are [made] in the Āhavanīya fire, because of Vedic text and designation.
Because the purpose is accomplished with taking [the offering] once.

1.9.m: Or both [methods] for all, because there is no specific rule.
Without cutting into pieces, each cutting is the size of the thumb-joint, from the middle and from the front half.
A measured amount in the case of curd and milk.
One less for the Sviṣṭakṛt offering.
After cutting the portion, replenishing with clarified butter is done prior to the Sviṣṭakṛt.
The call for the recitation [of the puronuvākyā] is according to the deity: "Recite for so-and-so."

1.9.s: praiṣānuvācane ṣaṣṭhi vapāyai \ dhānāsomebhyas \\ iti parihāpya //
1.9.d: प्रैषानुवाचने षष्ठि वपायै \ धानासोमेभ्यस् \\ इति परिहाप्य ॥
1.9.m: In the call (praiṣa) and the invitatory recitation (anuvācana), the genitive case [is used], except for the omentum [where the dative is used], [and except in the formula:] "for the fried barley grains and soma".

1.9.s: savaṣaṭkārāsu tiṣṭhan dakṣiṇata udaṅ prāṅ vaṣaṭkṛte //
1.9.d: सवषट्कारासु तिष्ठन् दक्षिणत उदङ् प्राङ् वषट्कृते ॥
1.9.m: At [offerings] accompanied by the vaṣaṭ-call, standing south [of the altar], facing north or east, when the vaṣaṭ has been uttered;
Ghee [is poured] on both sides of the sacrificial substance.

1.10.s: vartamānopadeśāc codanāśabdāchrutyarthābhāvāt tavai ceti vacanān nirdeśāt karmacodakaḥ //
1.10.d: वर्तमानोपदेशाच् चोदनाशब्दाछ्रुत्यर्थाभावात् तवै चेति वचनान् निर्देशात् कर्मचोदकः ॥
1.10.m: Because it is taught with a present tense, because of injunction words, because of the absence of a literal sense, because of the expression "and with -tavai", and because of specific designation, it is an enjoiner of action;
or it is a mantra, because of co-utterance.
Preparation of the substances [is done] according to the calculation of their purpose.
The skins have their hair turned upward and the neck directed eastward.
The lower [part of the animal's hide] is said to be the upper [layer] in the sacrificial substance.
When there is a single substance with ghee, supporting [the offering ladle] is done with the grass broom.

1.10.d: पाणिभ्यां जुहूं परिगृह्योपभृत्य् आधानम् आदानकाले ऽसम्̐ह्रादयन् ॥
1.10.m: Grasping the Juhū ladle with both hands, placing it upon the Upabhṛt ladle at the time of taking it, without clattering.
In the case of [actions] stated without a fruit, heaven [is the fruit], through inherent capacity.
In a single rite, when there is a particular auxiliary quality, there is a particular fruit.
In giving gifts, reciting, touching along, choosing boons, vows, and measures, one should understand the sacrificer [as the agent].
In the case of what is dug, cut off, severed, pounded, ground, milked, or burnt, [the formula applies] because the action enjoined by the yajus is possible.

1.10.s: raudram̐ rākṣasam āsuram ābhicaraṇikaṃ mantram uktvā pitryam ātmānaṃ cālabhyopaspṛśed apaḥ (upspṛśed apaḥ) //
1.10.d: रौद्रम्̐ राक्षसम् आसुरम् आभिचरणिकं मन्त्रम् उक्त्वा पित्र्यम् आत्मानं चालभ्योपस्पृशेद् अपः (उप्स्पृशेद् अपः) ॥
1.10.m: Having spoken a mantra addressed to Rudra, to the Rakṣases, to the Asuras, or of an sorcery nature, or one addressed to the Pitṛs, and having touched himself, he should touch water.

2.1.m: He should observe the fast on either the first full-moon day or the second.
The Adhvaryu priest or the sacrificer adds fuel to the fires.

2.1.s: mamāgne varco vihaveṣv astu \ vayaṃ tvendhānās tanvaṃ puṣema \ mahyaṃ namantāṃ pradiśaś catasras \ tvayādhyakṣeṇa pṛtanā jayema \\ ity āhavanīye samidham ādadhāti //
2.1.d: ममाग्ने वर्चो विहवेष्व् अस्तु \ वयं त्वेन्धानास् तन्वं पुषेम \ मह्यं नमन्तां प्रदिशश् चतस्रस् \ त्वयाध्यक्षेण पृतना जयेम \\ इत्य् आहवनीये समिधम् आदधाति ॥
2.1.m: He puts a firestick on the Āhavanīya fire with: "May splendor be mine, O Agni, in the rival invocations; may we, kindling you, nourish our bodies; may the four quarters bow down to me; with you as overseer, may we conquer the armies!"
Or [he adds fuel] with the Great Vyāhṛtis, concluding in the east;
During that day he should avoid meat and sexual intercourse.
He shaves his head and beard, or [leaves] the topknot.
In the afternoon, [the sacrificer and his wife] eat the fast-entering food, moderately sated with clarified butter.

2.1.s: antareṇāparāgnī gatvāpareṇāhavanīyaṃ prāṅ tiṣṭhann agnim īkṣamāṇo 'pa upaspṛśya vratam upaiti \\ agne vratapate \\ idam aham iti vā satyavādyataḥ //
2.1.d: अन्तरेणापराग्नी गत्वापरेणाहवनीयं प्राङ् तिष्ठन्न् अग्निम् ईक्षमाणो ऽप उपस्पृश्य व्रतम् उपैति \\ अग्ने व्रतपते \\ इदम् अहम् इति वा सत्यवाद्यतः ॥
2.1.m: Going between the two western fires, standing west of the Āhavanīya fire facing east, looking at the fire, and touching water, he undertakes the vow with: "O Agni, lord of vows!" or with: "Here I...", from that moment speaking the truth.
Speaking the truth is an auxiliary of the ritual subsequently.
Or he may eat [the produce] of trees and wild plants.
He sleeps on the ground in the Āhavanīya hall;

2.1.s: agnihotram̐ hutvā brahmāṇaṃ vṛṇīte brahmiṣṭham \\ bhūpate bhuvanapate mahato bhūtasya pate brahmāṇaṃ tvā vṛṇīmahe \\ iti //
2.1.d: अग्निहोत्रम्̐ हुत्वा ब्रह्माणं वृणीते ब्रह्मिष्ठम् \\ भूपते भुवनपते महतो भूतस्य पते ब्रह्माणं त्वा वृणीमहे \\ इति ॥
2.1.m: having offered the Agnihotra, he chooses as Brahman priest one most proficient in the Veda, with: "O lord of the earth, lord of the world, lord of the great being, we choose you as Brahman priest!"

2.1.s: vṛto japati \\ ahaṃ bhūpatir ahaṃ bhuvanapatir ahaṃ mahato bhūtasya patir \ bhūr bhuvaḥ svar \ deva savitar etaṃ tvā vṛṇate bṛhaspatiṃ brahmāṇam \ tad ahaṃ manase prabravīmi \ mano gāyatryai \ gāyatrī triṣṭubhe \ triṣṭub jagatyai \ jagaty anuṣṭubhe \\ anuṣṭup prajāpataye \ prajāpatir viśvebhyo devebhyas \\ bṛhaspatir devānāṃ brahmāhaṃ manuṣyāṇām iti //
2.1.d: वृतो जपति \\ अहं भूपतिर् अहं भुवनपतिर् अहं महतो भूतस्य पतिर् \ भूर् भुवः स्वर् \ देव सवितर् एतं त्वा वृणते बृहस्पतिं ब्रह्माणम् \ तद् अहं मनसे प्रब्रवीमि \ मनो गायत्र्यै \ गायत्री त्रिष्टुभे \ त्रिष्टुब् जगत्यै \ जगत्य् अनुष्टुभे \\ अनुष्टुप् प्रजापतये \ प्रजापतिर् विश्वेभ्यो देवेभ्यस् \\ बृहस्पतिर् देवानां ब्रह्माहं मनुष्याणाम् इति ॥
2.1.m: Having been chosen, he mutters: "I am the lord of the earth, I am the lord of the world, I am the lord of the great being. Bhūḥ, Bhuvaḥ, Svaḥ! O divine Savitṛ, they choose this Bṛhaspati as Brahman priest for you. That I announce to the mind; the mind to the Gāyatrī; the Gāyatrī to the Triṣṭubh; the Triṣṭubh to the Jagatī; the Jagatī to the Anuṣṭubh; the Anuṣṭubh to Prajāpati; Prajāpati to all the gods. Bṛhaspati is the Brahman priest of the gods; I am that of men."
He says: "O lord of speech, protect the sacrifice!"
He steps across to the south, behind the Āhavanīya fire.

2.1.s: ahe daidhiṣavyod atas tiṣṭhānyasya sadane sīda yo 'smat pākataras \\ iti brahmasadanam īkṣate //
2.1.d: अहे दैधिषव्योद् अतस् तिष्ठान्यस्य सदने सीद यो ऽस्मत् पाकतरस् \\ इति ब्रह्मसदनम् ईक्षते ॥
2.1.m: He looks at the seat of the Brahman priest with: "O son of a Daidhiṣavya, stand up from there! Sit on the seat of another who is less wise than we!"

2.1.s: brahmasadanāt tṛṇaṃ nirasyati nirastaḥ pāpmā saha tena yaṃ dviṣmas \\ iti //
2.1.d: ब्रह्मसदनात् तृणं निरस्यति निरस्तः पाप्मा सह तेन यं द्विष्मस् \\ इति ॥
2.1.m: He tosses away a blade of grass from the seat of the Brahman priest with: "Cast out is evil along with him whom we hate!"

2.1.s: idam ahaṃ bṛhaspateḥ sadasi sīdāmi \ prasūto devena savitrā \ tad agnaye prabravīmi \ tad vāyave \ tat pṛthivyai \\ iti //
2.1.d: इदम् अहं बृहस्पतेः सदसि सीदामि \ प्रसूतो देवेन सवित्रा \ तद् अग्नये प्रब्रवीमि \ तद् वायवे \ तत् पृथिव्यै \\ इति ॥
2.1.m: [He sits with:] "Here I sit in the seat of Bṛhaspati, impelled by the divine Savitṛ. That I announce to Agni, that to Vāyu, that to the earth."

2.2.m: He sits down on the seat of the Brahman priest, facing the Āhavanīya fire.
Restraining his speech until the impelling of the after-offerings;
If he utters [speech], he should mutter a mantra addressed to Viṣṇu.

2.2.s: praṇaya yajñam \\ devatā vardhaya tvam \\ nākasya pṛṣṭhe yajamāno astu \ saptaṛṣīṇām̐ sukṛtāṃ yatra lokas \ tatremaṃ yajñaṃ yajamānaṃ ca dhehi \\ o3ṃ praṇaya \\ iti praṇītāḥ prasauti //
2.2.d: प्रणय यज्ञम् \\ देवता वर्धय त्वम् \\ नाकस्य पृष्ठे यजमानो अस्तु \ सप्तऋषीणाम्̐ सुकृतां यत्र लोकस् \ तत्रेमं यज्ञं यजमानं च धेहि \\ ओ3ं प्रणय \\ इति प्रणीताः प्रसौति ॥
2.2.m: With: "Lead forth the sacrifice, increase the deities! May the sacrificer be upon the back of heaven; where is the realm of the seven righteous sages, there place this sacrifice and the sacrificer! Om, lead forth!" he impels the Praṇītā waters.
Thus addressed, [he responds] with the syllable Om.
With: "Sprinkle the sacrifice!", [he impels him] over the sacrificial substance;

2.2.s: bṛhaspate parigṛhāṇa vedim \\ sugā vo devāḥ sadanāni santu \\ asyāṃ barhiḥ prathatām̐ sādhv antar \ ahim̐srā pṛthivī devī devy astu \\ iti vediṃ parigṛhṇantam //
2.2.d: बृहस्पते परिगृहाण वेदिम् \\ सुगा वो देवाः सदनानि सन्तु \\ अस्यां बर्हिः प्रथताम्̐ साध्व् अन्तर् \ अहिम्̐स्रा पृथिवी देवी देव्य् अस्तु \\ इति वेदिं परिगृह्णन्तम् ॥
2.2.m: [He addresses him] while he encloses the altar with: "O Bṛhaspati, enclose the altar! May the seats be easy to reach for you, O gods! Within this may the sacrificial grass spread well; may the divine Earth be free from injury!"

2.2.d: प्रजापते ऽनुब्रूहि यज्ञम् इति सामिधेनीर् अनुवक्ष्यन्तम् ॥
2.2.m: With: "O Prajāpati, recite for the sacrifice!", [he addresses] him when he is about to recite the kindling verses.

2.2.s: mitrasya tvā cakṣuṣā pratīkṣe \\ iti prāśitraṃ pratīkṣate //
2.2.d: मित्रस्य त्वा चक्षुषा प्रतीक्षे \\ इति प्राशित्रं प्रतीक्षते ॥
2.2.m: He looks at the Prāśitra portion with: "I look upon you with the eye of Mitra."
He accepts it with: "At the [impulse] of the divine [Savitṛ]..."

2.2.s: pṛthivyās tvā \\ iti sādayaty apohya barhīm̐ṣi //
2.2.d: पृथिव्यास् त्वा \\ इति सादयत्य् अपोह्य बर्हीम्̐षि ॥
2.2.m: With the mantra, "On the lap of the earth [I set] thee...", he places it down, having pushed aside the blades of sacrificial grass.

2.2.s: punar ādāya devasya tvā \\ ity anāmikāṅguṣṭhābhyām agneṣ ṭvā \\ iti prāśnāti dantair anupaspṛśann atra cet //
2.2.d: पुनर् आदाय देवस्य त्वा \\ इत्य् अनामिकाङ्गुष्ठाभ्याम् अग्नेष् ट्वा \\ इति प्राश्नाति दन्तैर् अनुपस्पृशन्न् अत्र चेत् ॥
2.2.m: Taking it up again with the mantra, "At the impulse of the divine [Savitṛ]...", he eats it with the ring finger and thumb with the mantra, "To Agni [I offer] thee...", not touching it with his teeth, if it is to be consumed now.

2.2.s: prakṣālya pātraṃ nābhim ālabhate yā apsv antar devatās tā idam̐ śamayantu \ svāhākṛtaṃ jaṭharam indrasya gacha \ ghasinā me mā sampṛkthās \\ ūrdhvaṃ me nābheḥ sīda \\ indrasya tvā jaṭhare sādayāmi \\ iti //
2.2.d: प्रक्षाल्य पात्रं नाभिम् आलभते या अप्स्व् अन्तर् देवतास् ता इदम्̐ शमयन्तु \ स्वाहाकृतं जठरम् इन्द्रस्य गछ \ घसिना मे मा सम्पृक्थास् \\ ऊर्ध्वं मे नाभेः सीद \\ इन्द्रस्य त्वा जठरे सादयामि \\ इति ॥
2.2.m: Having rinsed the vessel, he touches his navel with the mantra: "May the deities who are within the waters appease this. Offered with Svāhā, go into the belly of Indra. Do not mingle with my bile; settle above my navel. I seat thee in the belly of Indra."
When addressed regarding the fuel stick, he gives permission with the formula: "This thy [fuel stick, O Lord of the earth]..."

2.2.s: karmāpavarge samidham ādadhāti juhoty upatiṣṭhate vā namaḥ kṛtāya karmaṇe \ akṛtāya karmaṇe namaḥ \ ayāḍ yajñaṃ jātavedās \\ antaraḥ pūrvo asmin niṣadya \ sa tvam̐ sanim̐ suvimucā vimuñca \ dhehy asmabhyaṃ draviṇaṃ jātavedaḥ svāhā \\ iti yathetam etya //
2.2.d: कर्मापवर्गे समिधम् आदधाति जुहोत्य् उपतिष्ठते वा नमः कृताय कर्मणे \ अकृताय कर्मणे नमः \ अयाड् यज्ञं जातवेदास् \\ अन्तरः पूर्वो अस्मिन् निषद्य \ स त्वम्̐ सनिम्̐ सुविमुचा विमुञ्च \ धेह्य् अस्मभ्यं द्रविणं जातवेदः स्वाहा \\ इति यथेतम् एत्य ॥
2.2.m: At the conclusion of the ritual, having returned by the way he came, he places a fuel stick [on the fire], offers an oblation, or attends [the fire] with the mantra: "Homage to the deed done; homage to the deed undone! Jātavedas has sacrificed for the sacrifice, seated inside as the first priest in this rite. As such, do thou release bounty by a good release; bestow wealth upon us, O Jātavedas, svāhā!"
This is the duty of the Brahman priest in the animal sacrifice and the primary archetype sacrifices.

2.3.s: gārhapatyam uttareṇodapātraṃ nidhāyālabhate bhūtas tvā bhūta kariṣyāmi \\ iti //
2.3.d: गार्हपत्यम् उत्तरेणोदपात्रं निधायालभते भूतस् त्वा भूत करिष्यामि \\ इति ॥
2.3.m: Having placed a water vessel north of the Gārhapatya fire, he touches it with the mantra: "Thou art becoming; I will make thee become."

2.3.s: brahmann apaḥ prṇeṣyāmi \ yajamāna vācaṃ yacha \\ ity āha //
2.3.d: ब्रह्मन्न् अपः प्र्णेष्यामि \ यजमान वाचं यछ \\ इत्य् आह ॥
2.3.m: He says: "O Brahman, I will fill the waters; O sacrificer, restrain your speech!"

2.3.s: anujñāta uttareṇāhavanīyam̐ samprati nidadhāti kas tvā \\ iti //
2.3.d: अनुज्ञात उत्तरेणाहवनीयम्̐ सम्प्रति निदधाति कस् त्वा \\ इति ॥
2.3.m: Permitted [by the Brahman], he sets it down directly north of the Āhavanīya fire with the mantra: "Who [fills] thee?"
[Vessels made] of bronze, wood, or clay [are used] respectively by those desiring sorcery, spiritual luster, or firm establishment.

2.3.s: tṛṇair agnīn paristrīya purastāt prathamaṃ dviśaḥ prātrāṇi sam̐sādayati //
2.3.d: तृणैर् अग्नीन् परिस्त्रीय पुरस्तात् प्रथमं द्विशः प्रात्राणि सम्̐सादयति ॥
2.3.m: Having enclosed the fires with grass, he arranges the utensils in pairs, starting from the east.

2.3.s: śūrpāgnihotrahavaṇi sphyakapālam̐ śamyākṛṣṇājinam ulūkhalamusalaṃ dṛṣadupalam arthavac ca //
2.3.d: शूर्पाग्निहोत्रहवणि स्फ्यकपालम्̐ शम्याकृष्णाजिनम् उलूखलमुसलं दृषदुपलम् अर्थवच् च ॥
2.3.m: The winnowing basket, the Agnihotra ladle, the wooden sword, the potsherds, the yoke-pin, the black antelope skin, the mortar and pestle, the upper and lower millstones, and whatever else is required.
[He places them] behind or to the north of the cooking fire.

2.3.s: karmaṇe vām iti śūrpāgnihotravaṇy ādāya vācaṃ yachati //
2.3.d: कर्मणे वाम् इति शूर्पाग्निहोत्रवण्य् आदाय वाचं यछति ॥
2.3.m: Taking the winnowing basket and the Agnihotra ladle with the mantra, "For the rite, [I take] you two...", he restrains his speech.
He heats them [over the fire] with the formula: "Scorched is [the demon]...", or "Burnt is [the demon]..."

2.3.s: gachati \\ urv antarikṣam iti śrapaṇasya paścād anas tiṣṭhat samaṅgi //
2.3.d: गछति \\ उर्व् अन्तरिक्षम् इति श्रपणस्य पश्चाद् अनस् तिष्ठत् समङ्गि ॥
2.3.m: He goes with the formula, "The wide atmosphere...", towards the cart that stands well-balanced behind the cooking fire.
Touching the yoke is done with the formula: "Thou art the yoke..."
[He touches] the pole behind the prop with the formula: "[Thou art the yoke] of the gods..."
The stepping onto [the cart] is done with the formula: "May Viṣṇu [stride over] thee..."
He looks at the oblation materials with the formula: "[Look upon] the wide [space] for the wind..."
He throws away any foreign matter with the formula: "Smitten away is [the demon]..."
He touches it with the formula: "May they stretch forth..."

2.3.s: devasya tvā \\ iti gṛhṇāty āgneyaṃ caturo muṣṭīn //
2.3.d: देवस्य त्वा \\ इति गृह्णात्य् आग्नेयं चतुरो मुष्टीन् ॥
2.3.m: With the formula, "At the impulse of the divine [Savitṛ]...", he takes four handfuls [of grain] for Agni.
Touching the remainder is done with the formula: "For prosperity, thee..."
He steps down with the formula: "Let [the poles] stand firm..."
He walks with the formula: "The wide atmosphere..."

2.3.s: śrapaṇasya paścāt sādayati pṛthivyās tvā \\ iti //
2.3.d: श्रपणस्य पश्चात् सादयति पृथिव्यास् त्वा \\ इति ॥
2.3.m: He sets it down behind the cooking fire with the formula: "On the earth's [lap I set] thee..."
Or in a trough placed upon the wooden sword.
He mutters the formulas for the yoke, pole, and mounting at the opening of the trough.
Rising is accompanied by the formula: "Let [the poles] stand firm..."

2.3.s: kuśau samāv apraśīrṇāgrāv anantargarbhau kuśaiś chinatti pavitre sthas \\ iti //
2.3.d: कुशौ समाव् अप्रशीर्णाग्राव् अनन्तर्गर्भौ कुशैश् छिनत्ति पवित्रे स्थस् \\ इति ॥
2.3.m: He cuts two blades of kuśa grass, equal in length, unbroken at their tips, and having no shoots inside, using [other] blades of kuśa, with the formula: "You two are strainers..."

2.3.s: havirgrahaṇyām apaḥ kṛtvā tābhyām utpunāti savitur vas \\ iti //
2.3.d: हविर्ग्रहण्याम् अपः कृत्वा ताभ्याम् उत्पुनाति सवितुर् वस् \\ इति ॥
2.3.m: Having poured water into the vessel for taking oblation-materials, he purifies it with those two [strainers] with the mantra: "[By the impulse] of Savitṛ, [I purify] you..."

2.3.s: savye kṛtvā dakṣiṇenodiṅgayati devīr āpas \\ iti //
2.3.d: सव्ये कृत्वा दक्षिणेनोदिङ्गयति देवीर् आपस् \\ इति ॥
2.3.m: Placing them in his left hand, he stirs [the water] upward with his right hand with the formula: "O divine waters..."
Sprinkling them is done with the formula: "You are sprinkled..."

2.3.s: haviś ca \\ agnaye tvā \\ agnīṣomābhyām tvā \\ iti //
2.3.d: हविश् च \\ अग्नये त्वा \\ अग्नीषोमाभ्याम् त्वा \\ इति ॥
2.3.m: And [he sprinkles] the sacrificial substance with the formulas: "To Agni, thee!", "To Agni-Soma, thee!"
Having placed the sprinkling waters where there is no crossing path;

2.4.m: Taking the black antelope skin is done with the formula: "Thou art protection..."
Stepping away from the utensils, he shakes it out with the formula: "Shaken out is [the demon]..."
He spreads it out with its neck pointing to the west, with the formula: "[Thou art] the skin of Aditi..."

2.4.s: savyāśūnye nidadhāty ulūkhalam adrir asi \ grāvāsi \\ iti vā //
2.4.d: सव्याशून्ये निदधात्य् उलूखलम् अद्रिर् असि \ ग्रावासि \\ इति वा ॥
2.4.m: On the left unoccupied part [of the skin], he places the mortar with the formula: "Thou art a rock...", or "Thou art a pressing-stone..."
He pours the oblation-grain into [the mortar] with the formula: "[Thou art] the body of Agni..."
When there are various seeds, [the release occurs] at the last one, because of competence.
He takes the pestle with the formula: "A large pressing-stone [art thou]..."
He summons three times with: “Preparer of the oblation, come!”
From then on, the wife threshes, or someone else.

2.4.s: āhvayaty āhanty anyo dṛṣadupale kukkuṭo 'si \\ iti triḥ śamyayā dvir dṛṣadam̐ sakṛd upalām //
2.4.d: आह्वयत्य् आहन्त्य् अन्यो दृषदुपले कुक्कुटो ऽसि \\ इति त्रिः शम्यया द्विर् दृषदम्̐ सकृद् उपलाम् ॥
2.4.m: While he calls, another strikes the lower and upper millstones with the wooden pin three times: twice the lower millstone, once the upper millstone, with: “You are a cock.”
He takes the winnowing basket with: “You are grown through rain.”
He pours out the oblation with: “To you…”
He winnows out with: “Blown away…”
He discards the husks with: “Struck away…”
He separates [the grains] with: “May Vāyu [separate] you…”
Having poured [them] into the vessel, he consecrates [them] with: “May the god [Savitṛ purify] you…”

2.4.s: devebhyaḥ śundhadhvam \\ devebhyaḥ śundhadhvam ity eke //
2.4.d: देवेभ्यः शुन्धध्वम् \\ देवेभ्यः शुन्धध्वम् इत्य् एके ॥
2.4.m: According to some, with: “Be pure for the gods! Be pure for the gods!”
Having polished [the grains], he sets aside the broken grains.
The grinding and the arranging [of the potsherds occur] simultaneously.

2.4.s: dhṛṣṭir asi \\ ity upaveṣam ādāya \\ apāgne \\ ity aṅgārān prācaḥ karoti //
2.4.d: धृष्टिर् असि \\ इत्य् उपवेषम् आदाय \\ अपाग्ने \\ इत्य् अङ्गारान् प्राचः करोति ॥
2.4.m: Having taken the poker with: “You are a fire-stirrer,” he pushes the burning embers eastward with: “O fire, push away…”

2.4.s: ā devayajam ity aṅgāram āhṛtya kapālenāvachādayati dhruvam asi \\ iti //
2.4.d: आ देवयजम् इत्य् अङ्गारम् आहृत्य कपालेनावछादयति ध्रुवम् असि \\ इति ॥
2.4.m: Having drawn an ember near with: “To the place of sacrifice to the gods…,” he covers it with a potsherd with: “You are firm.”
If practicing sorcery, [he replaces] the word for enemy with: “Of so-and-so.”

2.4.d: सव्याङ्गुल्याशून्ये ऽङ्गारं निदधाति \\ अग्ने ब्रह्म \\ इति ॥
2.4.m: In the [potsherd] not touching his left finger, he places an ember with: “O Agni, the sacred word…”
To the south with: “For all [the gods]…”

2.4.s: samaṃ vibhajya dve dakṣiṇata evam uttaratas \\ cita stha \\ iti //
2.4.d: समं विभज्य द्वे दक्षिणत एवम् उत्तरतस् \\ चित स्थ \\ इति ॥
2.4.m: Dividing equally, [he places] two on the south and similarly on the north with: “You are arranged.”
In the same manner, eleven [potsherds are arranged] for the [cake] to Agni-Soma.
He heaps embers around them with: “Of the Bhṛgus…”

2.5.m: He places the mixing waters on [the fire].
He takes the black antelope skin as before, [spreading it] over the [first] black antelope skin.
On it [he places] the lower millstone with: “You are the bowl.”
Behind it he pushes the wooden pin pointing northward with: “Of heaven…”
On the lower millstone [he places] the upper millstone with: “You are the bowl.”

2.5.s: dhānyam asi \\ iti taṇḍulān opya pinaṣṭi prāṇāya tvā \\ iti pratimantram //
2.5.d: धान्यम् असि \\ इति तण्डुलान् ओप्य पिनष्टि प्राणाय त्वा \\ इति प्रतिमन्त्रम् ॥
2.5.m: Having poured the grains with: “You are grain,” he grinds [them] with the respective mantras: “For your out-breath…”
He sweeps [the flour] forward onto the black antelope skin with: “A long [thread of life]…”

2.5.s: piṣyamāṇeṣu nirvapaty anyas \\ mahīnām ity ājyam //
2.5.d: पिष्यमाणेषु निर्वपत्य् अन्यस् \\ महीनाम् इत्य् आज्यम् ॥
2.5.m: While [the grains] are being ground, another pours out the clarified butter with: “Of the great…”

2.5.s: pātryām̐ sapavitrāyāṃ piṣṭāny āvapati devasya tvā \\ iti //
2.5.d: पात्र्याम्̐ सपवित्रायां पिष्टान्य् आवपति देवस्य त्वा \\ इति ॥
2.5.m: He pours the flour into a vessel containing strainers with: “At the impulse of god…”
He sits down behind the cooking fire, or inside the altar ground.
Another brings the mixing waters.
He receives [them] with two strainers with: “May the waters unite…”
He mixes [the dough] with: “For your production…”

2.5.s: samaṃ vibhajyāsam̐hariṣyann ālabhate \\ idam agner \ idam agnīṣomayor iti //
2.5.d: समं विभज्यासम्̐हरिष्यन्न् आलभते \\ इदम् अग्नेर् \ इदम् अग्नीषोमयोर् इति ॥
2.5.m: Dividing [the dough] equally, intending not to blend them, he touches [them] with: “This is for Agni; this is for Agni-Soma.”

2.5.s: iṣe tvā \\ ity ājyam adhiśrayaty anyaḥ //
2.5.d: इषे त्वा \\ इत्य् आज्यम् अधिश्रयत्य् अन्यः ॥
2.5.m: Another puts the clarified butter on [the fire] with: “For vigor, you!”
For one who has no wife, [the cooking takes place] on the Āhavanīya fire, for one who cooks thereon.
With: “You are the heat,” [he places] the sacrificial cake [on the potsherds] simultaneously.
With: “O broad-spreading one…,” he spreads it to the extent of the potsherds, not too thick.

2.5.s: agniṣ ṭe \\ ity adbhir abhimṛśati sakṛt trir vā //
2.5.d: अग्निष् टे \\ इत्य् अद्भिर् अभिमृशति सकृत् त्रिर् वा ॥
2.5.m: With: “May Agni [not burn] your [skin]…,” he touches it with water once or three times.

2.5.s: paryagnikaroti \\ antaritam̐ rakṣas \\ antaritā arātayas \\ iti sahājyam //
2.5.d: पर्यग्निकरोति \\ अन्तरितम्̐ रक्षस् \\ अन्तरिता अरातयस् \\ इति सहाज्यम् ॥
2.5.m: He carries fire around [it] together with the clarified butter with: “Hidden is the demon; hidden are the enemies.”

2.5.s: atamerur iti śṛtāv abhivāsayati bhasmanā vedenopaveṣeṇaṃ vā //
2.5.d: अतमेरुर् इति शृताव् अभिवासयति भस्मना वेदेनोपवेषेणं वा ॥
2.5.m: With: “Free from languor…,” when it is cooked, he covers it with ashes by means of the grass broom or the poker.

2.5.s: pātryaṅguliprakṣālanam āptyebhyo ninayaty abhitapya pratyag asam̐syandamānam \\ tritāya tvā \\ iti pratimantram //
2.5.d: पात्र्यङ्गुलिप्रक्षालनम् आप्त्येभ्यो निनयत्य् अभितप्य प्रत्यग् असम्̐स्यन्दमानम् \\ त्रिताय त्वा \\ इति प्रतिमन्त्रम् ॥
2.5.m: Having heated the water used for washing the pan and fingers, he pours it out westward, not flowing together, for the Āptyas, with the respective mantra: “For Trita, you…”
He places the Anvāhārya [mess of rice] on the Dakṣiṇāgni fire.

2.6.m: West of the Āhavanīya fire he digs the altar.
[It is dug] up to the eradication of the roots of the plants.
He should direct: "Uproot the roots of the plants!"
For one desiring cattle, [the altar should be made] with loose earth brought [from elsewhere].

2.6.s: vediṃ parisamuhya vitṛtīye 'gnīd uttarata utkaraṃ karoti //
2.6.d: वेदिं परिसमुह्य वितृतीये ऽग्नीद् उत्तरत उत्करं करोति ॥
2.6.m: Having swept around the altar, the Agnīdh makes the rubbish heap in the north, at the [northern] third part.

2.6.s: devasya tvā \\ iti sphyam ādāya satṛṇam̐ savye kṛtvā dakṣiṇenālabhya japati \\ indrasya bāhur iti //
2.6.d: देवस्य त्वा \\ इति स्फ्यम् आदाय सतृणम्̐ सव्ये कृत्वा दक्षिणेनालभ्य जपति \\ इन्द्रस्य बाहुर् इति ॥
2.6.m: Having taken the wooden sword with "[At the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins, with the hands of Pūṣan,] of the god thee...", placing it along with a blade of grass in the left hand and touching it with the right, he mutters: "Indra's arm [thou art]...".
About to carry the stambayajus, he should not touch the earth nor himself with it.

2.6.s: vedyāṃ tṛṇaṃ nidadhāty udak pṛthivyai varmāsi \\ iti //
2.6.d: वेद्यां तृणं निदधात्य् उदक् पृथिव्यै वर्मासि \\ इति ॥
2.6.m: He places a blade of grass on the altar toward the north with: "Thou art the armour of the earth."

2.6.d: पृथिवि देवयजनि \\ इति तृणे ऽन्तर्हिते प्रहरति ॥
2.6.m: When the blade of grass has intervened, he strikes with: "O earth, place of divine sacrifice!"
He takes the loose earth with: "Go to the enclosure!"
He looks at the altar with: "May [the sky] rain for thee!"
He places [it] upon the rubbish heap with: "Tie [the knot]!".
Or [the blade of grass is carried away] remaining with what was struck, because of an unqualified instruction.
The second [carrying of earth, beginning with] striking, etc., is done with: "Araru [hath fled]..."

2.6.s: abhinyasyaty agnīd utkaram araro divam iti //
2.6.d: अभिन्यस्यत्य् अग्नीद् उत्करम् अररो दिवम् इति ॥
2.6.m: The Agnīdh throws down [the earth] upon the rubbish heap with: "Araru [shall] not [fly to] the sky!"
The fourth [is done] silently, with a blade of grass.

2.6.s: pūrvaṃ parigrahaṃ parigṛhṇāti dakṣiṇataḥ paścād uttarataś ca sphyena gāyatreṇa \\ iti pratimantram //
2.6.d: पूर्वं परिग्रहं परिगृह्णाति दक्षिणतः पश्चाद् उत्तरतश् च स्फ्येन गायत्रेण \\ इति प्रतिमन्त्रम् ॥
2.6.m: He makes the first enclosure [of the altar] to the south, west, and north with the wooden sword, each with its respective mantra, beginning with: "With the Gāyatrī [metre]...".

2.6.s: vedyāṃ trir ullikhyāha hara trir iti //
2.6.d: वेद्यां त्रिर् उल्लिख्याह हर त्रिर् इति ॥
2.6.m: Having drawn three lines on the altar, he says: "Carry [earth] three times!"
Having carried [it], the Agnīdh touches the lines.
In the sacrifice to the ancestors and in the fire altar piling [this occurs].
The preparation of the altar is as stated [in the Brāhmaṇa].

2.6.s: uttaraṃ parigrahaṃ parigṛhṇāti sukṣmā \ syonā \\ ūrjasvatī \\ iti pratimantraṃ pūrvavat //
2.6.d: उत्तरं परिग्रहं परिगृह्णाति सुक्ष्मा \ स्योना \\ ऊर्जस्वती \\ इति प्रतिमन्त्रं पूर्ववत् ॥
2.6.m: He makes the second enclosure with: "Thou art easy of access...", "thou art pleasant...", "thou art full of sap...", each with its respective mantra, as before.
He rubs along [the altar lines] with: "Before the cruel [slaughter]...".
Another [priest] holds the sprinkling waters closely over the altar.

2.6.s: atha sphyam udyamyāha prokṣaṇīr āsādaya \\ idhmaṃ barhir upasādaya \ srucaḥ saṃmṛḍḍhi \ patnīm̐ saṃnahya \\ ājyenodehi \\ iti yadīchet //
2.6.d: अथ स्फ्यम् उद्यम्याह प्रोक्षणीर् आसादय \\ इध्मं बर्हिर् उपसादय \ स्रुचः संमृड्ढि \ पत्नीम्̐ संनह्य \\ आज्येनोदेहि \\ इति यदीछेत् ॥
2.6.m: Then, having raised the wooden sword, he says: "Set down the sprinkling waters! Place the fuel bundle and sacrificial grass! Cleanse the ladles! Gird the wife! Come up with the clarified butter!" — if he wishes.
Another [performs] as commanded, because it belongs to another's sphere of duty.
Before the strewing [of the grass], he should not touch the altar with his hand,
nor the cooked oblations until the time of performance.
Some cut off [the oblation portions] with the thumb and fingers joined at the fleshy parts.
Strewing [the grass], he should throw aside whatever is defective.

2.6.s: dviṣato badhas \\ iti sphyam udañcaṃ praharati //
2.6.d: द्विषतो बधस् \\ इति स्फ्यम् उदञ्चं प्रहरति ॥
2.6.m: He throws the wooden sword northward with: "The slaughter of the enemy [art thou]!".

2.6.s: avanijya pāṇī apareṇa praṇītā sphyaṃ nidadhāti //
2.6.d: अवनिज्य पाणी अपरेण प्रणीता स्फ्यं निदधाति ॥
2.6.m: Having washed his hands, he lays down the wooden sword to the west of the Praṇītā waters.
And the fuel bundle and the sacrificial grass [he sets down], first the fuel bundle.
Or having brought [them] to the south of the Praṇītā waters.

2.6.s: sruvaṃ pratapya pūrvavad vedāgrair antarataḥ prāk saṃmārṣṭi \\ aniśitas \\ iti viparyasya bahir mūlaiḥ prāṅ utkramya //
2.6.d: स्रुवं प्रतप्य पूर्ववद् वेदाग्रैर् अन्तरतः प्राक् संमार्ष्टि \\ अनिशितस् \\ इति विपर्यस्य बहिर् मूलैः प्राङ् उत्क्रम्य ॥
2.6.m: Having heated the dipping spoon, as before, he cleanses it inside toward the east with the tips of the grass broom with "unblunted...", [and] having reversed it, outside with the roots, having stepped forward toward the east.
Having heated each one repeatedly, he hands it over.
Silently [he cleanses] the Prāśitra vessel, the vessel for cooked portions, and the pan.
He throws away the sweepings [of grass blades used for cleansing].
Some [prescribe] throwing [them] into the Āhavanīya fire.

2.7.s: patnīm̐ saṃnahyati pratyagdakṣiṇata upaviṣṭāṃ gārhapatyasya muñjayoktreṇa trivṛtā pariharaty adhīvāsas \\ adityai rāsnā \\ iti //
2.7.d: पत्नीम्̐ संनह्यति प्रत्यग्दक्षिणत उपविष्टां गार्हपत्यस्य मुञ्जयोक्त्रेण त्रिवृता परिहरत्य् अधीवासस् \\ अदित्यै रास्ना \\ इति ॥
2.7.m: He girds the wife seated to the south-west of the Gārhapatya fire; with a three-strand cord of muñja grass he wraps [her] around outside her upper garment with: "The girdle of Aditi [art thou]...".

2.7.s: dakṣiṇaṃ pāśam uttare pratimucyordhvam udgūhati viṣṇor veṣyas \\ iti //
2.7.d: दक्षिणं पाशम् उत्तरे प्रतिमुच्योर्ध्वम् उद्गूहति विष्णोर् वेष्यस् \\ इति ॥
2.7.m: Having fastened the right loop in the left, he tucks it upward with: "Thou art the garment of Viṣṇu!".

2.7.s: ūrje tvā \\ ity ājyam udvāsya patnīm avekṣayati \\ adabdhena \\ iti //
2.7.d: ऊर्जे त्वा \\ इत्य् आज्यम् उद्वास्य पत्नीम् अवेक्षयति \\ अदब्धेन \\ इति ॥
2.7.m: Having taken down the clarified butter [from the fire] with: "For sap thee!", he causes the wife to look at [it] with: "With an undeceivable [eye]...".
He places [the clarified butter] on the altar to the west of the sprinkling waters.
Or for those who cook it on the Āhavanīya, having prepared it on the Āhavanīya fire.
He purifies the clarified butter with: "[By the impulse of] Savitṛ thee...".
He looks at the clarified butter with: "Thou art splendour!".

2.7.s: caturjuhvām \\ dhāma nāma \\ iti sakṛn mantraḥ //
2.7.d: चतुर्जुह्वाम् \\ धाम नाम \\ इति सकृन् मन्त्रः ॥
2.7.m: Four times into the Juhū ladle; the mantra: "Domain, name..." is [uttered] once.
Eight times into the Upabhṛt ladle, if the after-offerings are fewer [than usual];
four times elsewhere, because of the division [of the offerings],
and because [the distinction] is seen in the animal sacrifice and the guest reception.
[This is so] because of a specific textual statement in the case of the animal sacrifice and the guest offering.

2.7.s: idhmaṃ prokṣati visram̐sya vediṃ ca barhiḥ pratigṛhya vedyāṃ kṛtvā purastādgranthi kṛṣṇo 'si \\ iti pratimantram //
2.7.d: इध्मं प्रोक्षति विस्रम्̐स्य वेदिं च बर्हिः प्रतिगृह्य वेद्यां कृत्वा पुरस्ताद्ग्रन्थि कृष्णो ऽसि \\ इति प्रतिमन्त्रम् ॥
2.7.m: Having untied [it], he sprinkles the fuel bundle and the altar with water, takes up the sacrificial grass, places it upon the altar with its knot to the east, with a mantra for each [action]: 'You are Kṛṣṇa...'
He pours the remainder [of the sprinkling water] at the roots [of the sacrificial grass] with: 'Aditi's moistening...'

2.7.s: pavitre nidhāya praṇītāsu barhir visram̐sya purastāt prastaragrahaṇam \\ viṣṇor iti //
2.7.d: पवित्रे निधाय प्रणीतासु बर्हिर् विस्रम्̐स्य पुरस्तात् प्रस्तरग्रहणम् \\ विष्णोर् इति ॥
2.7.m: Having placed the two purifying strainers into the Praṇītā water and untied the sacrificial grass, he takes the Prastara bunch from the eastern end with: 'Viṣṇu's...'

2.7.s: brahmaṇe pradāya saṃnahanaṃ visram̐sya dakṣiṇasyāṃ vediśroṇau nidhāyānyair avachādya vedim̐ stṛṇāti \\ ūrṇamradasam iti trivṛt //
2.7.d: ब्रह्मणे प्रदाय संनहनं विस्रम्̐स्य दक्षिणस्यां वेदिश्रोणौ निधायान्यैर् अवछाद्य वेदिम्̐ स्तृणाति \\ ऊर्णम्रदसम् इति त्रिवृत् ॥
2.7.m: Having given the cord to the Brahman, untied it, and laid it down at the southern hip of the altar, covering it with other [blades of grass], he strews the altar threefold with: 'Soft as wool...'
At this point occurs the removal [from the fire] of that which was cooked on the Āhavanīya fire.

2.7.s: idhmāt samidham ādāyāhavanīyaṃ kalpayaty uparyupari prastaraṃ dhārayan //
2.7.d: इध्मात् समिधम् आदायाहवनीयं कल्पयत्य् उपर्युपरि प्रस्तरं धारयन् ॥
2.7.m: Taking a kindling stick from the fuel bundle, he arranges the Āhavanīya fire, holding the Prastara bunch higher and higher above it.
He pushes back two burning embers, if there are to be after-offerings.

2.8.s: paridhīn paridadhāty ārdrān ekavṛkṣīyān bāhumātrān pālāśavaikaṅkatakārṣmaryabailvān pūrvālābhepūrvālābha uttarān khādiraudumbarān vā madhyamadakṣiṇottarān gandharvas \\ iti pratimantram //
2.8.d: परिधीन् परिदधात्य् आर्द्रान् एकवृक्षीयान् बाहुमात्रान् पालाशवैकङ्कतकार्ष्मर्यबैल्वान् पूर्वालाभेपूर्वालाभ उत्तरान् खादिरौदुम्बरान् वा मध्यमदक्षिणोत्तरान् गन्धर्वस् \\ इति प्रतिमन्त्रम् ॥
2.8.m: He lays down the enclosing sticks—wet, from a single tree, an arm's length, made of Palāśa, Vikaṅkata, Kārṣmarya, or Bilva; in the absence of each earlier one, the subsequent one; or of Khadira or Udumbara: middle, southern, and northern, with the mantra 'The Gandharva...' for each.

2.8.s: prathamaṃ paridhim̐ samidhopaspṛśya vītihotram ity ādadhāti //
2.8.d: प्रथमं परिधिम्̐ समिधोपस्पृश्य वीतिहोत्रम् इत्य् आदधाति ॥
2.8.m: Having touched the first enclosing stick with a kindling stick, he places [it] with: 'Invited to the feast...'
Without touching, [he places] the second [kindling stick] with: 'You are a kindling stick...'

2.8.s: sūryas tvā \\ iti japaty āhavanīyam īkṣamāṇas tadvacanatvāt //
2.8.d: सूर्यस् त्वा \\ इति जपत्य् आहवनीयम् ईक्षमाणस् तद्वचनत्वात् ॥
2.8.m: He mutters: 'May Sūrya [protect] you...', looking at the Āhavanīya fire, because [the mantra] addresses it.

2.8.s: āvṛtya vediṃ barhiṣas tṛṇe tiraścī nidadhāti savitur iti //
2.8.d: आवृत्य वेदिं बर्हिषस् तृणे तिरश्ची निदधाति सवितुर् इति ॥
2.8.m: Turning around the altar, he places two blades of sacrificial grass crosswise with: 'Savitṛ's...'
And when desiring to place the sacrificial cake and the curds.
He spreads the Prastara bunch upon the two [grass-blades] with: 'Soft as wool...'
He presses it down with: 'May the Vasus [sit upon] you...'

2.8.s: savyāśūnye juhūṃ pratigṛhya nidadhāti ghṛtācī \\ iti //
2.8.d: सव्याशून्ये जुहूं प्रतिगृह्य निदधाति घृताची \\ इति ॥
2.8.m: Holding the Juhū ladle so that his left hand is not empty, he sets it down with: 'O glowing with ghee...'

2.8.s: evam itare uttarābhyāṃ pratimantraṃ barhiṣy upabhṛtaṃ dhurvāṃ cāvakṛṣṭe 'nupūrvam //
2.8.d: एवम् इतरे उत्तराभ्यां प्रतिमन्त्रं बर्हिष्य् उपभृतं धुर्वां चावकृष्टे ऽनुपूर्वम् ॥
2.8.m: Likewise the other two with the subsequent two mantras, one for each: the Upabhṛt upon the sacrificial grass, and the Dhruvā drawn further back, in order.

2.8.s: puroḍāśāv abhighāryodvāsyopastīrṇe nidhāyānakti yas te prāṇaḥ paśuṣu praviṣṭas >\\ devānāṃ viṣṭhām anu yo vitasthe \ ātmanvānt soma ghṛtavān hi bhūtvā \\ agniṃ gacha svar yajamānāya vinda \\ iti //
2.8.d: पुरोडाशाव् अभिघार्योद्वास्योपस्तीर्णे निधायानक्ति यस् ते प्राणः पशुषु प्रविष्टस् >\\ देवानां विष्ठाम् अनु यो वितस्थे \ आत्मन्वान्त् सोम घृतवान् हि भूत्वा \\ अग्निं गछ स्वर् यजमानाय विन्द \\ इति ॥
2.8.m: Having poured clarified butter over the two sacrificial cakes, taken them off [the fire], and placed them on [the grass] strewn beneath, he anoints them with: 'Whatever breath of yours entered into the animals, which spread following the distribution of the gods; endowed with breath, O Soma, having become rich in ghee, go to Agni, win heaven for the sacrificer.'

2.8.s: pratyanakti kapālāni yāni gharme kapālāni \\ upacinvanti vedhasaḥ \ pūṣṇas tāny api vrate \\ indravāyū vimuñcatām iti //
2.8.d: प्रत्यनक्ति कपालानि यानि घर्मे कपालानि \\ उपचिन्वन्ति वेधसः \ पूष्णस् तान्य् अपि व्रते \\ इन्द्रवायू विमुञ्चताम् इति ॥
2.8.m: He anoints the potsherds in return: 'The potsherds which in the hot season the wise arrange, may Indra and Vāyu release them also according to Pūṣan's rule.'

2.8.s: priyeṇa dhāmnā \\ iti havīm̐ṣi vedyāṃ kṛtvā dhruvā asadann iti sarvāṇy ālabhate //
2.8.d: प्रियेण धाम्ना \\ इति हवीम्̐षि वेद्यां कृत्वा ध्रुवा असदन्न् इति सर्वाण्य् आलभते ॥
2.8.m: Having placed the offerings on the altar with: 'By your dear abode...', he touches all of them with: 'Firm they have sat...'
Or here occurs the entering upon the observance.

3.1.s: hotṛṣadanaṃ kṛtvāpareṇa vedim̐ śroṇiṃ vottareṇedhmāt samidham ādāya \\ agnaye samidhyamānāyānubrūhi \\ ity āha //
3.1.d: होतृषदनं कृत्वापरेण वेदिम्̐ श्रोणिं वोत्तरेणेध्मात् समिधम् आदाय \\ अग्नये समिध्यमानायानुब्रूहि \\ इत्य् आह ॥
3.1.m: Having made the seat for the Hotṛ priest behind the altar or north of the hip, and taking a kindling stick from the fuel bundle, he says: 'Recite for Agni being kindled.'
[The recitation is] in the first tone-register before the Sviṣṭakṛt offering.

3.1.s: saṃtanvann iva me 'nubrūhi \\ ity āha yajamānaḥ //
3.1.d: संतन्वन्न् इव मे ऽनुब्रूहि \\ इत्य् आह यजमानः ॥
3.1.m: The sacrificer says: 'Recite for me continuously, as it were.'

3.1.s: aṅguṣṭhābhyāṃ cāvabādhate pādyābhyāṃ vā \\ idam aham amum avabādhe \\ iti dveṣyam //
3.1.d: अङ्गुष्ठाभ्यां चावबाधते पाद्याभ्यां वा \\ इदम् अहम् अमुम् अवबाधे \\ इति द्वेष्यम् ॥
3.1.m: And with both thumbs or with both big toes he presses down the hated enemy with: 'Here do I press down so-and-so.'
In the absence [of a specific enemy, he says]: 'the one hating [me],' or 'the rival.'

3.1.s: yāvatsāmidheni veda \\ idam ahaṃ tāvatithena vajreṇa \\ iti //
3.1.d: यावत्सामिधेनि वेद \\ इदम् अहं तावतिथेन वज्रेण \\ इति ॥
3.1.m: As many kindling verses [he knows, he strikes] with the grass broom: 'Here do I [strike him] with a thunderbolt of such-and-such number.'
The placing [of a kindling stick takes place] at each praṇava.

3.1.s: samiddhas \\ iti prāg ataḥ sarvam idhmam ekavarjam anuyājāś cet //
3.1.d: समिद्धस् \\ इति प्राग् अतः सर्वम् इध्मम् एकवर्जम् अनुयाजाश् चेत् ॥
3.1.m: Before [the verse beginning] 'Enkindled...', all the fuel sticks except one, if there are to be after-offerings.

3.1.s: anuvacanānte vedenāhavanīyaṃ trir upavājya sruveṇa pūrvam āghāram āghāryāha \\ agnim agnīt saṃmṛḍḍhi \\ iti //
3.1.d: अनुवचनान्ते वेदेनाहवनीयं त्रिर् उपवाज्य स्रुवेण पूर्वम् आघारम् आघार्याह \\ अग्निम् अग्नीत् संमृड्ढि \\ इति ॥
3.1.m: At the end of the recitation, having fanned the Āhavanīya fire thrice with the grass broom, and having poured the first continuous butter libation with the dipping spoon, he says: 'Agnīdh, cleanse the fire.'

3.1.s: idhmasaṃnahanair anuparidhi saṃmārṣṭi \\ agne vājajid iti tristriḥ parikrāmam //
3.1.d: इध्मसंनहनैर् अनुपरिधि संमार्ष्टि \\ अग्ने वाजजिद् इति त्रिस्त्रिः परिक्रामम् ॥
3.1.m: With the cords of the fuel bundle he cleanses along the enclosing sticks with: 'O Agni, conqueror of booty...', three times each, walking around.

3.1.s: aparam āhavanīyād añjaliṃ karoti namo devebhyaḥ svadhā pitṛbhyas \\ iti dakṣiṇata uttānam //
3.1.d: अपरम् आहवनीयाद् अञ्जलिं करोति नमो देवेभ्यः स्वधा पितृभ्यस् \\ इति दक्षिणत उत्तानम् ॥
3.1.m: To the west of the Āhavanīya fire he makes folded hands with palms upward to the south, with: 'Homage to the gods; svadhā to the fathers.'

3.1.s: apa upaspṛśya suyame me \\ iti juhūpabhṛtāv ādāyottarāṃ juhūṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇātikrāmati \\ aṅghriṇā viṣṇo \\ iti //
3.1.d: अप उपस्पृश्य सुयमे मे \\ इति जुहूपभृताव् आदायोत्तरां जुहूं कृत्वा दक्षिणातिक्रामति \\ अङ्घ्रिणा विष्णो \\ इति ॥
3.1.m: Having touched water, and taking up the Juhū and Upabhṛt ladles with: 'Well-controlled for me...', placing the Juhū above, he steps across to the south with: 'With the foot of Viṣṇu...'
The movement of the one who is about to offer is behind the enclosing sticks.
[Stepping] from this side with the left [foot], and from that side with the right [foot].
Having halted with: '[Upon the lap of Aditi] rich in Vasus...'

3.2.m: He offers the second continuous butter libation with: 'From here Indra...'

3.2.s: āghāryāsam̐sparśayant srucāv etya juhvā dhruvām̐ samanakti saṃ jyotiṣā \\ iti //
3.2.d: आघार्यासम्̐स्पर्शयन्त् स्रुचाव् एत्य जुह्वा ध्रुवाम्̐ समनक्ति सं ज्योतिषा \\ इति ॥
3.2.m: Having poured the libation, coming back without letting the two ladles touch each other, he anoints the Dhruvā ladle with the Juhū ladle with: 'Together with light...'
Having put [them] down and taken the cords of the fuel bundle, he says: 'Make [him] hear!'
Some [say he does so] having snapped off a blade of sacrificial grass from the altar or a chip of the fuel stick.
Thus everywhere in calls and responses.

3.2.s: atha pravṛṇīte \\ agnir devo daivyo hotā devān yakṣad vidvāṃś cikitvān manuṣvad bharatavad amuvad amuvad iti yajamānārṣeyāṇy āha parastād arvāñci trīṇi //
3.2.d: अथ प्रवृणीते \\ अग्निर् देवो दैव्यो होता देवान् यक्षद् विद्वांश् चिकित्वान् मनुष्वद् भरतवद् अमुवद् अमुवद् इति यजमानार्षेयाण्य् आह परस्ताद् अर्वाञ्चि त्रीणि ॥
3.2.m: Then he chooses [the Hotṛ priest]: 'May Agni, the divine Hotṛ priest, sacrifice to the gods, knowing and discerning, like Manu, like Bharata, like so-and-so, like so-and-so'; he recites the ancestral ṛṣis of the sacrificer, three [in number], descending from the remote ancestor downwards.
Or as many as are the composers of the mantras.
And [this is] obligatory for a Kṣatriya and a Vaiśya.

3.2.s: brahmaṇvad ā ca vakṣad \ brāhmaṇā asya yajñasya prāvitāras \\ asau mānuṣas \\ iti hotṛnām agrahaṇam //
3.2.d: ब्रह्मण्वद् आ च वक्षद् \ ब्राह्मणा अस्य यज्ञस्य प्रावितारस् \\ असौ मानुषस् \\ इति होतृनाम् अग्रहणम् ॥
3.2.m: 'Accompanied by prayer may he bring [them] hither; the Brahmins are the protectors of this sacrifice; so-and-so is the human [Hotṛ]'—thus [follows] the mention of the name of the Hotṛ priest.

3.2.s: agnir hotā \\ iti srugādāpanaṃ prayājeṣu saṃnidheḥ //
3.2.d: अग्निर् होता \\ इति स्रुगादापनं प्रयाजेषु संनिधेः ॥
3.2.m: 'Agni is the Hotṛ'—thus is the causing to take up the ladles, because of their proximity at the fore-offerings.

3.2.s: ghṛtavatīm ity ukte srucāv ādāyātikramyāśrāvyāha samidho yaja \\ iti //
3.2.d: घृतवतीम् इत्य् उक्ते स्रुचाव् आदायातिक्रम्याश्राव्याह समिधो यज \\ इति ॥
3.2.m: When [the Hotṛ] says: 'The ladle filled with ghee', [the Adhvaryu priest,] having taken the two ladles, having stepped across, and having called for the response, says: 'Offer to the fuel sticks.'
Or stepping forward before each one.
Without touching [the brim], he pours [the ghee] from the Upabhṛt ladle into the Juhū ladle for the fourth [fore-offering].

3.2.s: uttarāṃ juhūm adhyuhya prācīm avahṛtya juhoti //
3.2.d: उत्तरां जुहूम् अध्युह्य प्राचीम् अवहृत्य जुहोति ॥
3.2.m: Having raised the Juhū ladle higher and brought it down toward the east, he offers.

3.3.s: eko mamaikā tasya yo 'smān dveṣṭi yaṃ ca vayaṃ dviṣmas \\ ity evaṃ mithunair yathāsaṃkhyam //
3.3.d: एको ममैका तस्य यो ऽस्मान् द्वेष्टि यं च वयं द्विष्मस् \\ इत्य् एवं मिथुनैर् यथासंख्यम् ॥
3.3.m: 'One is mine, one is his who hates us and whom we hate'—thus in pairs corresponding to the number [of the fore-offerings].

3.3.s: na tasya kiṃ cana \\ iti pañcame //
3.3.d: न तस्य किं चन \\ इति पञ्चमे ॥
3.3.m: 'Nothing is his'—at the fifth [fore-offering].

3.3.s: tviṣimān \ apacitimān \ yaśasvī \<brahmavarcasī >\\ annādas \\ iti ca //
3.3.d: त्विषिमान् \ अपचितिमान् \ यशस्वी \<ब्रह्मवर्चसी >\\ अन्नादस् \\ इति च ॥
3.3.m: And: 'Possessed of radiance', 'Possessed of reverence', 'Possessed of renown', 'Possessed of holy luster', 'An eater of food'.
For additional [offerings, the mantras are inserted] after the fourth and fifth, because of their place.
Or after the first and fourth, according to their characteristic marks.
Or all [additional offerings] with the last one, because it is an auxiliary.

3.3.s: etya juhvābhighāraṇaṃ dhruvāyā haviṣa upabhṛtaś ca //
3.3.d: एत्य जुह्वाभिघारणं ध्रुवाया हविष उपभृतश् च ॥
3.3.m: Having returned, the basting [is done] with the Juhū ladle of the Dhruvā ladle, of the sacrificial substance, and of the Upabhṛt ladle.
He performs the two ghee portions: the one to Agni and the one to Soma.
A fourfold cutting [is made] in [the offerings] that have a vaṣaṭ-call.

3.3.s: anidhāyāvadāyāvadāya dhruvām abhighārayati \\ āpyāyatāṃ dhruvā haviṣā ghṛtena \ yajñaṃyajñaṃ prati devayadbhyaḥ \ sūryāyā ūdho adityā upasthe \\ urudhārā pṛthivī yajñe asminn iti //
3.3.d: अनिधायावदायावदाय ध्रुवाम् अभिघारयति \\ आप्यायतां ध्रुवा हविषा घृतेन \ यज्ञंयज्ञं प्रति देवयद्भ्यः \ सूर्याया ऊधो अदित्या उपस्थे \\ उरुधारा पृथिवी यज्ञे अस्मिन्न् इति ॥
3.3.m: Without setting down [the ladle], cutting each time, he bastes the Dhruvā ladle with: 'May the Dhruvā ladle swell with sacrificial ghee, sacrifice after sacrifice, for those who seek the gods; in the lap of Aditi, the udder of Sūryā, may the earth of wide streams [swell] in this sacrifice.'

3.3.s: anubrūhi \\ ity uktvā nāpavyāhared dhotā cāśrāvaṇāt //
3.3.d: अनुब्रूहि \\ इत्य् उक्त्वा नापव्याहरेद् धोता चाश्रावणात् ॥
3.3.m: Having said: 'Recite [the invitatory verse]', neither [the Adhvaryu priest] should speak amiss nor the Hotṛ priest, until the calling for the response.
When the call for the response has been made, the Agnīdh priest [must not speak amiss] until his response.
When the response has been made, the Adhvaryu priest [must not speak amiss] until the direction to the Hotṛ priest.
And at the Soma [sacrifice], having drawn the soma cup, until the introductory chant;
when the chant is introduced, the Udgātṛ priests [must not speak amiss] until the direction to the Hotṛ priest;
[He offers] the [portion] to Agni in the northeastern half [of the fire].
The [portion] to Soma in the southeastern half.
Between the two sacrificial cakes, the [portion] to Agni-Soma of ghee [is offered] in a whisper.
Or [the deity is] Viṣṇu at the new moon, because of the prescription for the Hotṛ's office.
From whatever sacrificial substance [there is, a cutting] for Sviṣṭakṛt [is taken] from the northern half.

3.4.s: saṃcaram abhyukṣya prāśitram avadyati yavamātraṃ pippalamātraṃ vā //
3.4.d: संचरम् अभ्युक्ष्य प्राशित्रम् अवद्यति यवमात्रं पिप्पलमात्रं वा ॥
3.4.m: and having sprinkled the passage, he cuts the Brahman's portion of the size of a barley corn or of the size of a pippala berry.

3.4.s: adhvaryusaṃcareṇa brahmaṇe pradāya pūrveṇaike 'pa upaspṛśyeḍāṃ pañcāvattāṃ dakṣiṇato madhyāc ca yāvaddhaviḥ sviṣṭakṛdvad ājyam //
3.4.d: अध्वर्युसंचरेण ब्रह्मणे प्रदाय पूर्वेणैके ऽप उपस्पृश्येडां पञ्चावत्तां दक्षिणतो मध्याच् च यावद्धविः स्विष्टकृद्वद् आज्यम् ॥
3.4.m: Having given [it] to the Brahman priest along the Adhvaryu's path—according to some, by the front—and having touched water, [he cuts] the Iḍā fivefold, from the south and from the center, from whatever sacrificial substance [there is], and the ghee as in the case of Sviṣṭakṛt.

3.4.s: yajamānabhāgaṃ pūrvārdhād dīrghaṃ praśīrya purastād dhruvāyāḥ karoti //
3.4.d: यजमानभागं पूर्वार्धाद् दीर्घं प्रशीर्य पुरस्ताद् ध्रुवायाः करोति ॥
3.4.m: Having broken off the sacrificer's portion lengthwise from the eastern half, he places it in front of the Dhruvā ladle.
Having given the Iḍā to the Hotṛ priest without letting go [of it], he steps across to the south.
Having received the Iḍā, he anoints the two joints of the Hotṛ's fingers.
He places the intermediate Iḍā as before.

3.4.s: iḍopahūtā \\ ity ucyamāna āgneyaṃ barhiṣadaṃ karoti bradhna pinvasva \\ āyur me dhukṣva \ prajāṃ me dhukṣva \ paśūn me dhukṣva \ brahma me dhukṣva \ kṣatraṃ me dhukṣva \ viśo me dhukṣva \ yo 'smān dveṣṭi yaṃ ca vayaṃ dviṣmas tasya prajayā paśubhir āpyāyasva \\ iti taṃ caturdhā kṛtvā //
3.4.d: इडोपहूता \\ इत्य् उच्यमान आग्नेयं बर्हिषदं करोति ब्रध्न पिन्वस्व \\ आयुर् मे धुक्ष्व \ प्रजां मे धुक्ष्व \ पशून् मे धुक्ष्व \ ब्रह्म मे धुक्ष्व \ क्षत्रं मे धुक्ष्व \ विशो मे धुक्ष्व \ यो ऽस्मान् द्वेष्टि यं च वयं द्विष्मस् तस्य प्रजया पशुभिर् आप्यायस्व \\ इति तं चतुर्धा कृत्वा ॥
3.4.m: While 'iḍopahūtā...' is being recited, he makes [the cake] for Agni sit upon the barhis, having divided it into four parts, [with]: 'O sun, swell! Yield me life! Yield me offspring! Yield me cattle! Yield me spiritual power! Yield me lordly power! Yield me the commoners! May you swell through the offspring and cattle of him who hates us and whom we hate!'
He assigns [the portions] on the barhis to the officiating priests.
The sacrificer whispers: 'Here, O fathers...'
Having released [his hold], [he whispers]: 'They have rejoiced...'
At the invocation of Heaven and Earth, a sixfold portion [is brought] for the agnīdh.
He eats it with: 'The earth is invoked...'
The sacrificer whispers: 'Praying, may I [attain] this...'
The joined [priests] consume the invoked [iḍā].

3.4.s: pavitrayor mārjayante 'pareṇa vedim \\ sumitriyā nas \\ iti //
3.4.d: पवित्रयोर् मार्जयन्ते ऽपरेण वेदिम् \\ सुमित्रिया नस् \\ इति ॥
3.4.m: They cleanse themselves behind the altar across the two strainers, with: 'May [the waters] be friendly to us...'

3.4.s: yajamānasya prāṇāpānau pātam iti prastare te karoti //
3.4.d: यजमानस्य प्राणापानौ पातम् इति प्रस्तरे ते करोति ॥
3.4.m: He puts them on the prastara bunch with: 'Protect the out-breath and in-breath of the sacrificer.'
Or at this point the brahman eats [his portion].
He carries the portion around to him.
And the sacrificer's portion, if he has not gone away on a journey.

3.4.s: anvāhāryam abhighāryodvāsyāntarā brahmayajamānau hṛtvā vedyāṃ nidhāyālabhate prajāpater bhāgo 'sy ūrjasvān payasvān \ prāṇāpānau me pāhi \ samānavyānau me pāhi \\ udānavyānau me pāhi \\ ūrg asi \\ ūrjaṃ me dhehi \\ akṣitir asi mā me kṣeṣṭhā amutrāmuṣmiṃ loka iha ca \\ iti //
3.4.d: अन्वाहार्यम् अभिघार्योद्वास्यान्तरा ब्रह्मयजमानौ हृत्वा वेद्यां निधायालभते प्रजापतेर् भागो ऽस्य् ऊर्जस्वान् पयस्वान् \ प्राणापानौ मे पाहि \ समानव्यानौ मे पाहि \\ उदानव्यानौ मे पाहि \\ ऊर्ग् असि \\ ऊर्जं मे धेहि \\ अक्षितिर् असि मा मे क्षेष्ठा अमुत्रामुष्मिं लोक इह च \\ इति ॥
3.4.m: Having basted the anvāhārya cooked rice, taken it down, carried it between the brahman and the sacrificer, and placed it on the altar, he touches it [with]: 'You are Prajāpati's portion, full of vigor, full of milk. Protect my out-breath and in-breath! Protect my equal-breath and diffused-breath! Protect my up-breath and diffused-breath! You are vigor; bestow vigor upon me! You are imperishable; do not perish for me in that world over there nor here!'

3.5.s: samasyolmuke samidham ādāyāha brahman prasthāsyāmi \ *samidham ādhāyāgnim agnīt saṃmṛḍḍhi \\ iti //
3.5.d: समस्योल्मुके समिधम् आदायाह ब्रह्मन् प्रस्थास्यामि \ *समिधम् आधायाग्निम् अग्नीत् संमृड्ढि \\ इति ॥
3.5.m: Having united the two burning coals and taken a kindling stick, he says: 'O brahman, I shall set forth; having placed the kindling stick on the fire, O agnīdh, cleanse the fire!'
The hotṛ recites the accompaniment with: 'This is your [kindling stick]...'

3.5.s: saṃmārṣṭi pūrvavad aparikrāmam̐ sakṛtsakṛt sasṛvām̐sam iti //
3.5.d: संमार्ष्टि पूर्ववद् अपरिक्रामम्̐ सकृत्सकृत् ससृवाम्̐सम् इति ॥
3.5.m: Without stepping around, he wipes [the fire] once each time, as before, along with the dipping spoon.

3.5.d: ब्रह्मानुज्ञातो ऽनुयाजैस् त्रिभिश् चरत्य् औपभृतम्̐ समानीय ॥
3.5.m: Permitted by the brahman, he performs the three after-offerings, having poured in [butter] from the upabhṛt ladle.
Having stepped across and called for response, he says: 'Sacrifice to the gods!'
Or 'To the gods, to the gods!' everywhere, because of the restrictive expression.
Having poured [ghee] in for the fourth time, towards the east.

3.5.s: abhicarann anuyājānumantraṇam aśany amuṃ jahi \ hrāḍuny amuṃ jahi \\ ulkuṣy amuṃ jahi \\ iti //
3.5.d: अभिचरन्न् अनुयाजानुमन्त्रणम् अशन्य् अमुं जहि \ ह्राडुन्य् अमुं जहि \\ उल्कुष्य् अमुं जहि \\ इति ॥
3.5.m: When performing sorcery, the accompaniment for the after-offerings is: 'O lightning bolt, slay so-and-so! O hailstone, slay so-and-so! O fireball, slay so-and-so!'
Thus in the case of increase, he should divide equally.
Or by means of the final [mantra] of its own place, because of being the means.
Having returned, he unyokes the juhū and upabhṛt ladles.
[With]: 'Of Agni and Soma...', [he moves] the juhū eastwards with the right hand facing upwards.
[With]: 'May Agni and Soma [protect] him...', [he moves] the other [ladle] westwards with the other [hand] turned downwards.

3.5.s: anūjjayatv ayaṃ yajamānas \\ vājasyainam iti pūrve //
3.5.d: अनूज्जयत्व् अयं यजमानस् \\ वाजस्यैनम् इति पूर्वे ॥
3.5.m: 'May this sacrificer conquer following...', and 'Through vigor, him...' are the earlier [words].

3.5.s: yam ayaṃ yajamāno dveṣṭi yaś cainaṃ dveṣṭi \\ ity uttare //
3.5.d: यम् अयं यजमानो द्वेष्टि यश् चैनं द्वेष्टि \\ इत्य् उत्तरे ॥
3.5.m: 'Whom this sacrificer hates and who hates him...' are the later [words].

3.5.s: abhyukṣya juhvā paridhīn anakti yathāpūrvam \\ vasubhyas \\ iti pratimantram //
3.5.d: अभ्युक्ष्य जुह्वा परिधीन् अनक्ति यथापूर्वम् \\ वसुभ्यस् \\ इति प्रतिमन्त्रम् ॥
3.5.m: Having sprinkled [them] with water, he anoints the enclosing sticks with the juhū in proper order, with 'To the Vasus...', per each mantra.

3.6.s: prathamaṃ paridhiṃ gṛhītvāśrāvyāha \\ iṣitā daivyā hotāro bhadravācyāya preṣito mānuṣaḥ sūktavākāya \ sūktā brūhi \\ iti //
3.6.d: प्रथमं परिधिं गृहीत्वाश्राव्याह \\ इषिता दैव्या होतारो भद्रवाच्याय प्रेषितो मानुषः सूक्तवाकाय \ सूक्ता ब्रूहि \\ इति ॥
3.6.m: Having taken hold of the first enclosing stick and called for response, he says: 'The divine hotṛ priests have been urged to declare auspiciousness; the human [hotṛ] has been urged for the sūktavāka recitation: recite the hymns!'

3.6.s: paśau preṣya \\ iti //
3.6.d: पशौ प्रेष्य \\ इति ॥

3.6.s: saṃjānāthām iti prastarādānam //
3.6.d: संजानाथाम् इति प्रस्तरादानम् ॥
3.6.m: Taking the prastara bunch is done with: 'May the two of you agree...'

3.6.s: vidhṛtī sthāne kṛtvānakty enam \\ vyantu vayas \\ iti //
3.6.d: विधृती स्थाने कृत्वानक्त्य् एनम् \\ व्यन्तु वयस् \\ इति ॥
3.6.m: Having put the two separator-blades in position, he anoints it with: 'May the birds consume...'

3.6.s: agraṃ juhvām //
3.6.d: अग्रं जुह्वाम् ॥

3.6.s: upabhṛti madhyam //
3.6.d: उपभृति मध्यम् ॥

3.6.s: mūlam itarasyām //
3.6.d: मूलम् इतरस्याम् ॥

3.6.s: marutām iti nīcair hṛtvā tṛṇam ādāyānupraharati //
3.6.d: मरुताम् इति नीचैर् हृत्वा तृणम् आदायानुप्रहरति ॥
3.6.m: Having carried it downwards with [the formula] of the Maruts, and taking a blade of grass, he throws it into the fire after [it].

3.6.s: hastenācarati //
3.6.d: हस्तेनाचरति ॥

3.6.s: yajamānabhāgaṃ ca proṣite //
3.6.d: यजमानभागं च प्रोषिते ॥
3.6.m: And the sacrificer's portion when he is away on a journey.

3.6.s: kṣatriyavaiśyayoś ca nityam //
3.6.d: क्षत्रियवैश्ययोश् च नित्यम् ॥
3.6.m: And constantly in the case of a kṣatriya and a vaiśya.

3.6.s: ahaṃ tvad asmi mad asi tvam etat \\ mama tvaṃ yonis tava yonir asmi \ mamaiva san divi deveṣv adhi \ putraḥ pitrye lokakṛj jātavedaḥ svāhā \\ iti //
3.6.d: अहं त्वद् अस्मि मद् असि त्वम् एतत् \\ मम त्वं योनिस् तव योनिर् अस्मि \ ममैव सन् दिवि देवेष्व् अधि \ पुत्रः पित्र्ये लोककृज् जातवेदः स्वाहा \\ इति ॥
3.6.m: [With]: 'I am from you, you are from me, this; you are my womb, I am your womb; being mine alone in heaven above among the gods, a son in the world of the fathers, an author of the world, O Jātavedas, svāhā!'

3.6.s: sūktavākānte //
3.6.d: सूक्तवाकान्ते ॥

3.6.s: agnīd āha \\ anuprahara \\ iti //
3.6.d: अग्नीद् आह \\ अनुप्रहर \\ इति ॥

3.6.s: prāsya tṛṇam \\ cakṣuṣpās \\ ity ātmānam ālabhate //
3.6.d: प्रास्य तृणम् \\ चक्षुष्पास् \\ इत्य् आत्मानम् आलभते ॥
3.6.m: Having thrown in the blade of grass, he touches himself with: 'Eye-protector...'

3.6.s: saṃvadasva \\ agān agnīd \ agan \\ śrāvaya \ śrauṣaṭ \ svagā daivyā hotṛbhyaḥ \ svastir mānuṣebhyaḥ \ śamyor brūhi \\ ity eteṣām \\ saṃvadasva \\ agan \\ śrauṣaḍ ity agnīcheṣam itaro vyatyāsaṃ brūtaḥ //
3.6.d: संवदस्व \\ अगान् अग्नीद् \ अगन् \\ श्रावय \ श्रौषट् \ स्वगा दैव्या होतृभ्यः \ स्वस्तिर् मानुषेभ्यः \ शम्योर् ब्रूहि \\ इत्य् एतेषाम् \\ संवदस्व \\ अगन् \\ श्रौषड् इत्य् अग्नीछेषम् इतरो व्यत्यासं ब्रूतः ॥
3.6.m: Of these [dialogue formulas]: 'Converse with [me],' 'Has [Agni] gone, Agnīdh?', 'He has gone,' 'Call [it] out,' 'May he hear,' 'Svagā, divine ones, to the Hotṛs,' 'Blessing to the human ones,' 'Pronounce the Śaṃyu,' the Agnīdh recites 'Converse with [me],' 'He has gone,' and 'May he hear'; the other recites the rest in alternation.

3.6.s: paridhīn anupraharati yaṃ paridhim iti prathamam itarau ca yugapad agneḥ priyam iti //
3.6.d: परिधीन् अनुप्रहरति यं परिधिम् इति प्रथमम् इतरौ च युगपद् अग्नेः प्रियम् इति ॥
3.6.m: He throws in the enclosing sticks: the first with 'Which enclosing stick...', and the other two simultaneously with 'Dear to Agni...'.

3.6.s: srucau pragṛhṇāti sam̐sravabhāgās \\ iti sam̐sravān juhoti //
3.6.d: स्रुचौ प्रगृह्णाति सम्̐स्रवभागास् \\ इति सम्̐स्रवान् जुहोति ॥
3.6.m: He takes up both ladles and offers the remnants with: 'Sharers of the remnants...'.

3.6.s: ghṛtācī iti dhuri nidadhāty anasi ced grahaṇam //
3.6.d: घृताची इति धुरि निदधात्य् अनसि चेद् ग्रहणम् ॥
3.6.m: He places [them] on the pole [of the cart] with 'O ghee-bearing ones...', if the taking [of the grain] was from a cart.

3.6.s: sphye pātryāṃ cet //
3.6.d: स्फ्ये पात्र्यां चेत् ॥

3.6.s: yajña namaś ca te \\ iti vedim ālabhate //
3.6.d: यज्ञ नमश् च ते \\ इति वेदिम् आलभते ॥
3.6.m: He touches the altar with: 'O sacrifice, homage to you...'

3.6.s: vedam̐ hotā sruksruvam adhvaryur ājyasthālīm agnīd ādāya //
3.6.d: वेदम्̐ होता स्रुक्स्रुवम् अध्वर्युर् आज्यस्थालीम् अग्नीद् आदाय ॥
3.6.m: The Hotṛ having taken the grass broom, the Adhvaryu the ladle and dipping spoon, and the Agnīdh the clarified butter pot,

3.7.m: they go to the Gārhapatya fire for the Patnīsaṃyāja offerings.
The Adhvaryu, having approached the Gārhapatya fire to the east and south,
[or] to the west between the wife, according to some [teachers],
and having sat down, bending his right knee,
— in this manner in all seated oblations —

3.7.s: yajati somaṃ tvaṣṭāraṃ devānāṃ patnīragniṃ gṛhapatimiti //
3.7.d: यजति सोमं त्वष्टारं देवानां पत्नीरग्निं गृहपतिमिति ॥
3.7.m: He performs yajati-offerings to Soma, to Tvaṣṭṛ, to the wives of the gods, and to Agni Gṛhapati.
At the third [offering], there is a screening in front.
The wife touches the Adhvaryu from behind.
It ends with the Śaṃyu formula, or ends with the Iḍā.

3.7.s: śamyvante vedatṛṇam ādāyānakti prastaravat sruci sruve sthālyāṃ ca //
3.7.d: शम्य्वन्ते वेदतृणम् आदायानक्ति प्रस्तरवत् स्रुचि स्रुवे स्थाल्यां च ॥
3.7.m: If it ends with the Śaṃyu, having taken a blade of grass from the grass broom, he anoints it, as [he did] with the prastara, in the ladle, the dipping spoon, and the pot.
The throwing in of the blade of grass and the rest are as before.

3.7.d: शम्य्वन्ते स्रुक्स्रुवं प्रगृह्णाति \\ अग्ने ऽदब्धायो \\ इति ॥
3.7.m: If it ends with the Śaṃyu, he takes up the ladle and the dipping spoon with: 'O Agni of inviolable life...'.

3.7.s: savyenāvṛtya dakṣiṇāgnau juhoti \\ agnaye \\ iti sarasvatyai \\ iti ca //
3.7.d: सव्येनावृत्य दक्षिणाग्नौ जुहोति \\ अग्नये \\ इति सरस्वत्यै \\ इति च ॥
3.7.m: Turning to the left, he offers in the southern fire with: 'To Agni...', and with: 'To Sarasvatī...'.

3.7.s: ulūkhale musale yac ca śūrpe \\ āśiśleṣa dṛṣadi yat kapāle \ utpruṣo vipruṣaḥ saṃjuhomi \ satyāḥ santu yajamānasya kāmāḥ svāhā \\ iti piṣṭalepān juhoti //
3.7.d: उलूखले मुसले यच् च शूर्पे \\ आशिश्लेष दृषदि यत् कपाले \ उत्प्रुषो विप्रुषः संजुहोमि \ सत्याः सन्तु यजमानस्य कामाः स्वाहा \\ इति पिष्टलेपान् जुहोति ॥
3.7.m: With 'Whatever adhered to the mortar, to the pestle, and to the winnowing basket, whatever to the grinding stone and to the potsherd, I offer up these spurts and drops; may the desires of the sacrificer be true, svāhā,' he offers the flour remnants.

3.8.d: पत्नी वेदं प्रमुञ्चति वेदो ऽसि \\ इति ॥
3.8.m: The wife unfastens the grass broom with: 'You are the grass broom...'

3.8.s: yoktraṃ ca pra mā muñcāmi varuṇasya pāśāt \\ yena mābadhnāt savitā suśevaḥ \ ṛtasya yonau sukṛtasya loke \ ariṣṭāṃ mā saha patyā dadhātu \\ iti //
3.8.d: योक्त्रं च प्र मा मुञ्चामि वरुणस्य पाशात् \\ येन माबध्नात् सविता सुशेवः \ ऋतस्य योनौ सुकृतस्य लोके \ अरिष्टां मा सह पत्या दधातु \\ इति ॥
3.8.m: and the girdle with: 'I release myself from Varuṇa's bond, / with which Savitṛ the kindly bound me; / in the lap of cosmic order, in the world of virtuous deeds, / may he place me uninjured together with my husband.'

3.8.s: dhrauvam̐ samiṣṭayajur juhoti devā gātuvidas \\ iti //
3.8.d: ध्रौवम्̐ समिष्टयजुर् जुहोति देवा गातुविदस् \\ इति ॥
3.8.m: He offers the Samiṣṭayajus from the Dhruvā ladle with: 'O gods who know the path...'.

3.8.s: vedyāṃ praṇītā ninayati parītya kas tvā \\ iti //
3.8.d: वेद्यां प्रणीता निनयति परीत्य कस् त्वा \\ इति ॥
3.8.m: Having walked around, he pours out the praṇītā water onto the altar with: 'Who [pours] you?...'

3.8.s: puroḍāśakapālena kaṇān apāsyaty adhaḥkṛṣṇājinam \\ rakṣasām iti //
3.8.d: पुरोडाशकपालेन कणान् अपास्यत्य् अधःकृष्णाजिनम् \\ रक्षसाम् इति ॥
3.8.m: With the cake potsherd he discards the grains underneath the black antelope skin with: '[Share] of the Rakṣases...'.
Having walked around, he pours out the full vessel in a continuous stream.

3.8.d: यजमानो ऽञ्जलिना प्रतिगृह्णाति सं वर्चसा \\ इति ॥
3.8.m: The sacrificer receives [it] with folded hands with: 'Together with luster...'

3.8.s: viṣṇukramān kramate divi viṣṇur iti pratimantram //
3.8.d: विष्णुक्रमान् क्रमते दिवि विष्णुर् इति प्रतिमन्त्रम् ॥
3.8.m: He strides the Viṣṇu strides, one mantra per stride, with: 'In heaven Viṣṇu [strode]...'
Or upward from here with: 'On earth...'
He looks at the portion with: '[I look] from this food...'
at the earth with: 'For this firm foundation...'
at the Āhavanīya fire with: 'Together with radiant light...'

3.8.s: varcodās \\ iti yaṃ vā kāmaṃ kāmayate //
3.8.d: वर्चोदास् \\ इति यं वा कामं कामयते ॥
3.8.m: or whichever desire he desires with: 'Giver of luster...'
He turns clockwise with: '[Following the turn] of the sun...'
And silently at the drawing of soma cups, the answering recitations, and the offerings.
He attends upon the Gārhapatya fire with: 'O Agni, lord of the house...'
Or he may say: 'A hundred winters...'.
He turns clockwise with: '[Following the turn] of the sun...'
He goes eastward with: 'Wide, O Viṣṇu...'

3.8.s: tato 'si \ tantur asi \\ anu mā tanuhy asmin yajñe 'syām̐ sādhukṛtyāyām asminn anne 'smiṃ loke \\ idaṃ me karmedaṃ vīryaṃ putro 'nusaṃtanotu \\ iti putrasya nāma gṛhṇāti //
3.8.d: ततो ऽसि \ तन्तुर् असि \\ अनु मा तनुह्य् अस्मिन् यज्ञे ऽस्याम्̐ साधुकृत्यायाम् अस्मिन्न् अन्ने ऽस्मिं लोके \\ इदं मे कर्मेदं वीर्यं पुत्रो ऽनुसंतनोतु \\ इति पुत्रस्य नाम गृह्णाति ॥
3.8.m: With: 'You are extended; you are the thread; extend me along in this sacrifice, in this good deed, in this food, in this world; may my son extend this my rite, this my vigor,' he pronounces the name of his son.

3.8.s: tantave tvā jyotiṣe tvā \\ iti vā //
3.8.d: तन्तवे त्वा ज्योतिषे त्वा \\ इति वा ॥
3.8.m: Or with: 'To the thread you, to the light you...'
He attends upon the Āhavanīya fire silently.
He releases the observance with [the formula] with which he entered upon it.

3.8.s: saṃ yajñapatir āśiṣā \\ iti bhāgaṃ prāśnāti //
3.8.d: सं यज्ञपतिर् आशिषा \\ इति भागं प्राश्नाति ॥
3.8.m: He consumes his portion with: 'May the lord of sacrifice, with blessing...'

3.8.s: brāhmaṇaṃ tarpayitavai brūyād yajñam evaitat tarpayati \\ iti śruteḥ //
3.8.d: ब्राह्मणं तर्पयितवै ब्रूयाद् यज्ञम् एवैतत् तर्पयति \\ इति श्रुतेः ॥
3.8.m: He should order a brāhmaṇa to be satisfied [with food], because of the śruti: 'This indeed satisfies the sacrifice.'

4.1.m: In the afternoon on the new-moon day when the moon is not seen, [takes place] the Piṇḍapitṛyajña.
Having strewn [grass] around it, the placing of the implements [is done] one by one, as before.

4.1.s: apareṇa gārhapatyaṃ carum apūrṇam̐ srucaṃ vā tūṣṇīṃ gṛhītvottareṇa dakṣiṇāgnim avahanti tiṣṭhan //
4.1.d: अपरेण गार्हपत्यं चरुम् अपूर्णम्̐ स्रुचं वा तूष्णीं गृहीत्वोत्तरेण दक्षिणाग्निम् अवहन्ति तिष्ठन् ॥
4.1.m: Having silently taken, to the west of the Gārhapatya, a caru-pot or an unfilled sruc, he pounds [the grain] standing to the north of the Dakṣiṇāgni.

4.1.s: sārataṇḍulam apūrṇam̐ śrapayitvābhighāryodvāsya mekṣaṇena juhoti \\ agnaye \\ iti somāya \\ iti ca //
4.1.d: सारतण्डुलम् अपूर्णम्̐ श्रपयित्वाभिघार्योद्वास्य मेक्षणेन जुहोति \\ अग्नये \\ इति सोमाय \\ इति च ॥
4.1.m: Having cooked the substantial rice grains not completely full, having basted it [with clarified butter], and having removed it [from the fire], he offers with the stirring-stick [mekṣaṇa] saying, "To Agni..." and "To Soma..."

4.1.s: prāsya tad dakṣiṇenollikhati \\ apahatās \\ ity apareṇa vā //
4.1.d: प्रास्य तद् दक्षिणेनोल्लिखति \\ अपहतास् \\ इत्य् अपरेण वा ॥
4.1.m: Having thrown it [the mekṣaṇa] in, he draws a line to the south or to the west [of the fire] with [the mantra], "Slain are..."

4.1.s: ulmukaṃ parastāt karoti ye rūpāṇi \\ iti //
4.1.d: उल्मुकं परस्तात् करोति ये रूपाणि \\ इति ॥
4.1.m: He places a burning ember beyond [the line] with [the mantra], "Those forms which..."

4.1.s: udapātreṇāvanejayaty apasavyam̐ savyena voddharaṇasāmarthyād asāv avanenikṣva \\ iti yajamānasya pitṛprabhṛti trīn //
4.1.d: उदपात्रेणावनेजयत्य् अपसव्यम्̐ सव्येन वोद्धरणसामर्थ्याद् असाव् अवनेनिक्ष्व \\ इति यजमानस्य पितृप्रभृति त्रीन् ॥
4.1.m: With a water-pot, from right to left or with the left hand because of the competence of lifting, he makes three [ancestors] of the sacrificer, beginning with the father, wash their hands with [the formula], "N.N., wash yourself!"

4.1.s: upamūlam̐ sakṛdāchinnāni lekhāyāṃ kṛtvā yathāvaniktaṃ piṇḍān dadāti \\ asāv etat te \\ iti //
4.1.d: उपमूलम्̐ सकृदाछिन्नानि लेखायां कृत्वा यथावनिक्तं पिण्डान् ददाति \\ असाव् एतत् ते \\ इति ॥
4.1.m: Having placed grass stalks cut in a single stroke near the root upon the line, he offers the rice-balls (piṇḍas) in the same order as they washed, saying, "N.N., this is yours!"

4.1.s: ye ca tvām anu \\ iti caike //
4.1.d: ये च त्वाम् अनु \\ इति चैके ॥

4.1.s: atra pitaras \\ ity uktvodaṅṅ āsta ā tamanāt //
4.1.d: अत्र पितरस् \\ इत्य् उक्त्वोदङ्ङ् आस्त आ तमनात् ॥
4.1.m: Having said, "Here, O fathers...", he sits facing north until he ceases to breathe.
Turning back, he whispers, "They have gladdened themselves..."

4.1.s: avanejya pūrvavan nīviṃ visram̐sya namo vas \\ ity añjaliṃ karoti //
4.1.d: अवनेज्य पूर्ववन् नीविं विस्रम्̐स्य नमो वस् \\ इत्य् अञ्जलिं करोति ॥
4.1.m: Having made them wash as before, and having untied his waistband, he makes an añjali-gesture with [the mantra], "Homage to you..."

4.1.s: etad vas \\ ity upāsyati sūtrāṇi pratipiṇḍam //
4.1.d: एतद् वस् \\ इत्य् उपास्यति सूत्राणि प्रतिपिण्डम् ॥
4.1.m: With [the mantra], "This is for you...", he casts threads upon each rice-ball.
Or, in old age, hairs from the sacrificer's chest.
With [the mantra], "Sap...", he pours out water.
Having set [the rice-balls] down, the sacrificer smells them.
The burning ember and the once-cut stalks [are thrown] into the fire.

4.1.s: ādhatta \\ iti madhyamapiṇḍaṃ patnī prāśnāti putrakāmā //
4.1.d: आधत्त \\ इति मध्यमपिण्डं पत्नी प्राश्नाति पुत्रकामा ॥
4.1.m: The wife, desirous of a son, consumes the middle rice-ball with [the mantra], "Bestow..."
