For one whose father is living, [the rite] ends with the homa-offering, or there is no undertaking [of it at all].

4.1.s: na vyavete jātūkarṇyo na jīvantam atidadātīti śruteḥ //
4.1.d: न व्यवेते जातूकर्ण्यो न जीवन्तम् अतिददातीति श्रुतेः ॥
4.1.m: According to Jātūkarṇya, not when intervened, because of the Vedic text: "He does not give over a living one."
Or the Piṇḍapitṛyajña is performed beforehand, because of being a subsidiary rite [to the New-Moon sacrifice].
It is not a subsidiary rite, on account of the context, time, characteristic marks, favor-giving statements, and Vedic texts concerning the non-sacrificer of solemn fires (anāhitāgni).
Or it is a subsidiary rite, because of the simultaneous mention.

4.2.s: śvo nodetety adṛṣṭe vā parṇaśākhāṃ chinatti śāmīlīṃ vā \\ iṣe tvā \\ iti \\ ūrje tvā \\ iti vā //
4.2.d: श्वो नोदेतेत्य् अदृष्टे वा पर्णशाखां छिनत्ति शामीलीं वा \\ इषे त्वा \\ इति \\ ऊर्जे त्वा \\ इति वा ॥
4.2.m: With [the thought] 'Tomorrow it will not rise', or when [the moon] is not seen, he cuts a palāśa branch or a śamī branch with "For food thee!" or with "For vigor thee!"
Or [he adds] "I cut [thee]", because both [phrases] require a verb.
Or [he adds] "I bend [thee]" to the second.
[A branch] with many leaves, whose tip is not dry, pointing northeast or either [direction].

4.2.s: mātṛbhir vatsānt sam̐sṛjya vatsam̐ śākhyopaspṛśati vāyava stha \\ iti //
4.2.d: मातृभिर् वत्सान्त् सम्̐सृज्य वत्सम्̐ शाख्योपस्पृशति वायव स्थ \\ इति ॥
4.2.m: Having let the calves mix with the mothers, he touches a calf with the branch, saying, "You are Vāyus!"
Having separated one of the mothers with [the mantra], "May the god [Savitṛ drive] you..."
It belongs to Indra or to Mahendra.

4.2.s: yajamānasya paśūn ity agnyagārasyānyatarasya purastāchākhām upagūhati //
4.2.d: यजमानस्य पशून् इत्य् अग्न्यगारस्यान्यतरस्य पुरस्ताछाखाम् उपगूहति ॥
4.2.m: With [the mantra ending in], "...the cattle of the sacrificer", he hides the branch in front of either of the two fire-sheds.

4.2.d: मूलाद् उपवेषं करोति वेषो ऽसि \\ इति ॥
4.2.m: From the base [of the branch] he makes a fire-poker with [the formula], "Thou art the enterer [veṣa]."
[The branch is used] in the sāṃnāyya-offering because of the connection with the branch.

4.2.s: vasoḥ pavitram iti pavitramasyāṃ badhnāti kuśau //
4.2.d: वसोः पवित्रम् इति पवित्रमस्यां बध्नाति कुशौ ॥
4.2.m: With [the formula], "The purifier of the Vasu...", he ties a strainer of two kuśa blades to it [the milking pot].
For one offering the sāṃnāyya, the Agnihotra offering that night is of barley gruel.
When [the Agnihotra] is offered, he says, "Announce the [cow] that has been let loose [to the calf]!"
When it has been announced, the taking of the milk-pot [takes place] with [the formula], "Thou art the sky."
With [the mantra], "[The caul] of Mātariśvan...", he sets [the pot] on the fire.

4.2.s: vasoḥ pavitram iti pavitram asyāṃ karoty udag vā //
4.2.d: वसोः पवित्रम् इति पवित्रम् अस्यां करोत्य् उदग् वा ॥
4.2.m: With [the formula], "The purifier of the Vasu...", he places the strainer across it, or northward.
Restraining his speech, he causes [the cow] to be milked by a non-Śūdra.

4.2.s: sthālyanvārabdhe devas tvā \\ ity āsicyamāne japati //
4.2.d: स्थाल्यन्वारब्धे देवस् त्वा \\ इत्य् आसिच्यमाने जपति ॥
4.2.m: While touching the milk-pot, as [the milk] is being poured in, he whispers, "May the god thee..."
"Which one have you milked?" is the question.
When told, he says, "She is all-life."
In the same way [he does] with the other two [cows], with the subsequent two mantras, mantra by mantra.
His speech released, [he milks] the subsequent [cows] without touching [the pot].

4.2.s: parikṣālanam ānayati sampṛcyadhvam ṛtāvarīr \ ūrmiṇā madhumattamāḥ \ pṛñcatīr madhunā payas \\ mandrā dhanasya sātaye \\ iti //
4.2.d: परिक्षालनम् आनयति सम्पृच्यध्वम् ऋतावरीर् \ ऊर्मिणा मधुमत्तमाः \ पृञ्चतीर् मधुना पयस् \\ मन्द्रा धनस्य सातये \\ इति ॥
4.2.m: He pours the rinse-water [into the milk], with: "Mingle, O truthful ones, most sweet with wave, mingling milk with sweet, delightful, for the winning of wealth!"
Having removed [the milk] from the fire, he curdles [it] with the remainder of what was offered earlier, with: "Thee for Indra..."
He covers it with an earthen vessel [containing] water, with: "O Viṣṇu, [protect] the sacrificial offering!"
Having set [it] down, the driving away of the calves is as before.

4.2.d: प्रातर् आग्नेय ऐन्द्राग्नश् च द्वादशकपालो ऽसंनयतः ॥
4.2.m: In the morning, there is [a cake] on eight potsherds for Agni and one on twelve potsherds for Indra-Agni for one who does not offer the sāṃnāyya.
Having scooped out the clarified butter, the morning milking is [done] into another [pot].

4.2.s: parikṣālanāntaṃ kṛtvā sāyaṃdoham āhṛtya prātardoham̐ śrapayitvābhighāryodvāsyobhāv anakti //
4.2.d: परिक्षालनान्तं कृत्वा सायंदोहम् आहृत्य प्रातर्दोहम्̐ श्रपयित्वाभिघार्योद्वास्योभाव् अनक्ति ॥
4.2.m: Having carried out [the rites] up to the rinse-water, having brought the evening milking, having boiled the morning milking, basted it, and removed it from the fire, he anoints both.
Because of the Vedic text: "He cuts first from the boiled [milk]."
The moving apart [of the cakes] is done with: "[For] Indra and Agni..."
The throwing of the prastara-bunch [into the fire] is done together with the branch.

4.2.s: paridhibhiḥ sahopaveṣaṃ juhoti juhomi tvā subhaga saubhagāya \ purūtamaṃ puruhūta śravasyann iti //
4.2.d: परिधिभिः सहोपवेषं जुहोति जुहोमि त्वा सुभग सौभगाय \ पुरूतमं पुरुहूत श्रवस्यन्न् इति ॥
4.2.m: Together with the enclosing sticks, he offers the fire-stirring stick [with]: "I offer thee, fortunate one, for good fortune, thee invoked by many, O much-invoked one, seeking renown."
The rest is like the Full-Moon sacrifice, except for what is done on the same day.
One should sacrifice with the New- and Full-Moon sacrifices for thirty years;
[or] for fifteen [years] if he performs the Dākṣāyaṇayajña;
or he should just offer the Agnihotra [for life].

4.3.m: An action-word connected with a sacrificial substance and a deity is an offering designated by *yajati*.
The attributes of the New- and Full-Moon sacrifices apply to the animal sacrifices and [modified] brick/cake offerings (iṣṭi), because of fitness;
The attributes of the Vaiśvadeva apply to the Four-Month sacrifices, on account of explicit statements and ritual application;
and from the soma sacrifice to the avabhṛtha, because of the prohibition of sāmans;
not to the animal [sacrifice] like the grain-particles, because of the prescription of mantras;
in case of doubt, it is worldly, on account of improperness.
The specific rule in a ritual act [is determined] from commonalities of singular or dual designation, measure, sacrificial substance, deity, and secondary attributes.
When there is a conflict between sacrificial substance and deity, the restriction [favors] the sacrificial substance, because of its inherent relation [to the rite].
In the case of āmikṣā, [it belongs] to both, because it is produced from both.
That of the animal [belongs to that] of the sāṃnāyya: that has been stated;
[and] because of the milk's immediate proximity of time and accommodation of attributes.
Kāśakṛtsni holds that it is performed on the same day.
Vātsyabādarī holds that it is a restatement of the former.
Because of substitution among sacrificial substances, the acquisition of attributes is not contradicted.
Adaptation (ūha) according to sense [takes place] when [an archetype element is] enjoined;
not in the archetype rite, because of originality.
In a modified rite, non-application [of archetype details occurs] due to explicit injunction, cessation of purpose, or contradiction.
Since [subsidiaries] arise for the sake of another, where that is absent, there is absence [of the subsidiary];
In the contrary case, there would be no actions, because of co-mention.

4.4.m: The Dākṣāyaṇayajña is for one who desires offspring, cattle, food, and renown.
It is a distinct rite, on account of its having [its own] name, fruit, and secondary qualities;
or it is an injunction of secondary qualities, on account of proximity and the statement of attainment.
The offering to Agni-Soma is on the full-moon day;
On the new-moon day, there is curds-and-whey (payasyā) for Mitra-Varuṇa.

4.4.s: tatraiva dohanam̐ śṛte vā dadhy ānayati //
4.4.d: तत्रैव दोहनम्̐ शृते वा दध्य् आनयति ॥
4.4.m: The milking is done right there, or he pours curd into the boiled [milk].
Having poured off the whey, he puts it on the rubbish heap;
Having thrown a blade of grass [into it], he proceeds with it;
He scoops [the whey], sprinkling it over the sacrificial grass;
because of the Vedic text: "He thereby places semen into the bulls."

4.4.s: prativaṣaṭkāram̐ hutvā vājinaśeṣeṇa diśo vyāghārayati diśas \\ iti pratimantraṃ pradakṣiṇaṃ purastāt prathamam //
4.4.d: प्रतिवषट्कारम्̐ हुत्वा वाजिनशेषेण दिशो व्याघारयति दिशस् \\ इति प्रतिमन्त्रं प्रदक्षिणं पुरस्तात् प्रथमम् ॥
4.4.m: Having offered with the secondary vaṣaṭ-call, he sprinkles the quarters with the remainder of the whey, with the mantras to the quarters, sunwise, beginning in the east.
With the last two [mantras, he sprinkles] in the middle and in the eastern half.
The utterance of 'svāhā' [is added] everywhere, because [the mantras] require it.

4.4.s: śeṣam upahvayasya \\ ity āmantrayāmantrya bhakṣaṇam upahūtas \\ iti prasūtaḥ //
4.4.d: शेषम् उपह्वयस्य \\ इत्य् आमन्त्रयामन्त्र्य भक्षणम् उपहूतस् \\ इति प्रसूतः ॥
4.4.m: The consumption of the remainder [takes place] after repeatedly inviting with, 'Invite,' [and being] impelled with, 'You are invited.'
Or [only] in the common [rites], on account of suitability.

4.4.s: ṛtūnāṃ tvā vājināṃ vājinaṃ bhakṣayāmi \\ iti //
4.4.d: ऋतूनां त्वा वाजिनां वाजिनं भक्षयामि \\ इति ॥
4.4.m: [He consumes] with: 'Of the seasons, the swift ones, I consume the swift [whey].'
Or with: 'Full of vigor, invited, I consume the whey of the invited one.'
Or with: 'May I be vigorous in the contest.'
The Hotṛ, the Adhvaryu, the Brahman, the Agnīdh, and the sacrificer [consume it].
Or the sacrificer [consumes] first, or at both ends.
He should avoid meat, women, falsehood, and clothes stained with urine.

4.5.m: [The cake] for Savitṛ in the Four-Month sacrifices [is silent].
The deities of the Dīkṣaṇīyā, Prāyaṇīyā, and Ātithyā [rites are addressed silently].
The first [oblation] to Indra in the Sautrāmaṇī [is silent].
He may bring in the [cake] for Agni according to each desire.

4.5.s: varṣārthe prakṛtau vā brūyāt \\ vṛṣṭikāmo 'smi \\ iti //
4.5.d: वर्षार्थे प्रकृतौ वा ब्रूयात् \\ वृष्टिकामो ऽस्मि \\ इति ॥
4.5.m: Or in the archetype rite, for the sake of rain, he should say, 'I am desirous of rain.'

4.5.s: adhvaryuṃ brūyāt purovātaṃ ca vidyutaṃ ca manasā dhyāya \\ iti //
4.5.d: अध्वर्युं ब्रूयात् पुरोवातं च विद्युतं च मनसा ध्याय \\ इति ॥
4.5.m: He should say to the Adhvaryu: 'Meditate in your mind upon the east wind and lightning.'

4.5.s: stanayitnuṃ ca varṣaṃ ca \\ iti hotāram //
4.5.d: स्तनयित्नुं च वर्षं च \\ इति होतारम् ॥
4.5.m: To the Hotṛ: '[Meditate upon] thunder and rain.'
To the Brahman: '[Meditate upon] all these.'

4.5.s: anvārambhaṇīyāgnāvaiṣṇava ekādaśakapālaḥ sarasvatyai caruḥ sarasvate dvādaśakapālo darśapūrṇamāsārambhe //
4.5.d: अन्वारम्भणीयाग्नावैष्णव एकादशकपालः सरस्वत्यै चरुः सरस्वते द्वादशकपालो दर्शपूर्णमासारम्भे ॥
4.5.m: The Anvārambhaṇīyā [consists of] a cake on eleven potsherds to Agni-Viṣṇu, a pap to Sarasvatī, [and] a cake on twelve potsherds to Sarasvant, at the beginning of the New- and Full-Moon sacrifices.
A four-year-old cow is the sacrificial gift, or a pair [of cattle].
A cake on eleven potsherds to Indra Vimṛdh [is offered] following the Full-Moon sacrifice.
A pap to Aditi [is offered] following the New-Moon sacrifice.

4.6.s: āgrayaṇam aindrāgnam agrapākasya vrīhīṇāṃ yavānāṃ ca //
4.6.d: आग्रयणम् ऐन्द्राग्नम् अग्रपाकस्य व्रीहीणां यवानां च ॥
4.6.m: The Āgrayaṇa [first-fruits sacrifice consists of] a cake to Indra-Agni made from the first harvest of paddy or barley.
A cake on one potsherd to Dyāvāpṛthivī [is offered].
Having removed it [from the embers], he should cover its edges with clarified butter.
The firstborn calf is the sacrificial gift.

4.6.s: darśapūrṇamāsān ījāno dakṣiṇāgnipakvaṃ cātuṣprāśyaṃ brāhmaṇān bhojayet kiṃcid dadyāt //
4.6.d: दर्शपूर्णमासान् ईजानो दक्षिणाग्निपक्वं चातुष्प्राश्यं ब्राह्मणान् भोजयेत् किंचिद् दद्यात् ॥
4.6.m: One who has performed the New- and Full-Moon sacrifices should feed Brahmins with the four-portion pap cooked on the Dakṣiṇa fire, and should give something [as a gift].
For one performing the Agnihotrāyaṇa, the evening and morning Agnihotra oblation is made with new [grains].
At the Upasads, he should prepare the two Rauhiṇa cakes.
For wild grain, a pap of wild millet [is offered] to Soma.

4.6.s: punaḥsam̐skṛto ratho dakṣiṇā kṣaumaṃ madhuparko varṣādhṛtaṃ vā vāsaḥ //
4.6.d: पुनःसम्̐स्कृतो रथो दक्षिणा क्षौमं मधुपर्को वर्षाधृतं वा वासः ॥
4.6.m: A repaired chariot is the sacrificial gift, [or] linen cloth, honey-mixture, or a garment worn during the rainy season.

4.7.m: The setting up of the sacred fires [is performed] on a new-moon day.
Under the constellations Kṛttikās, Rohiṇī, Mṛgaśiras, or the Phalgunīs.
Spring [is the season] for a Brahmin and for one who desires spiritual lustre.
Summer for a Kṣatriya and for one who desires prosperity.
The rainy season for those who desire offspring or cattle, for a Vaiśya, and for a chariot-maker.
The shaving of the hair is as in the Full-Moon sacrifice.
When [the rite] is completed, they must be given to the Adhvaryu priest.
Having churned [fire] in the Gārhapatya shed, he sets it on [the hearth].
Or [he takes it] from the home of a Vaiśya, from an oven, or from a kitchen.

4.7.s: upāstamayam devāḥ pitaraḥ pitaro devās \\ *yo 'ham asmi sa san yaje \ yasyāham asmi na tam antarayāmi \ svaṃ ma iṣṭam̐ svam̐ śrāntam̐ svam̐ hutam astu \\ iti //
4.7.d: उपास्तमयम् देवाः पितरः पितरो देवास् \\ *यो ऽहम् अस्मि स सन् यजे \ यस्याहम् अस्मि न तम् अन्तरयामि \ स्वं म इष्टम्̐ स्वम्̐ श्रान्तम्̐ स्वम्̐ हुतम् अस्तु \\ इति ॥
4.7.m: Near sunset [he recites]: 'O gods who are the ancestors! O ancestors who are the gods! Being who I am, I sacrifice. Whose I am, from him I do not stray. May what I sacrifice, what I toil for, what I offer be my own!'
They sit down behind the fire, the wife to the south.
He hands over two kindling sticks made of an Aśvattha tree grown inside a Śamī tree.

4.7.s: vācaṃ yachā pūrṇāhuter ity āhāstamite niśāyām //
4.7.d: वाचं यछा पूर्णाहुतेर् इत्य् आहास्तमिते निशायाम् ॥
4.7.m: At sunset or at night, [the Adhvaryu] says: 'Restrain your speech until the full-spoon oblation!'
Or until sunrise, because that is the time of the primary rite.

4.8.m: He ties a he-goat in the Gārhapatya shed, or he does not.
If it is available, he should give it to the Agnīdh priest in the morning.

4.8.s: astamite rohite carmaṇy ānaḍuhe catvāri haviṣyapātrāṇi mimīte //
4.8.d: अस्तमिते रोहिते चर्मण्य् आनडुहे चत्वारि हविष्यपात्राणि मिमीते ॥
4.8.m: At sunset, upon a red ox-hide, he measures out four vessels of sacrificial food.
He cooks that [mess of rice] to be eaten by four [priests].

4.8.s: udvāsyāsecanaṃ madhye kṛtvā sarpir āsicyāśvatthīs tisraḥ samidho ghṛtāktā ādadhāti samidhāgnim iti pratyṛcam //
4.8.d: उद्वास्यासेचनं मध्ये कृत्वा सर्पिर् आसिच्याश्वत्थीस् तिस्रः समिधो घृताक्ता आदधाति समिधाग्निम् इति प्रत्यृचम् ॥
4.8.m: Having removed it from the fire, having made an indentation in the middle, and having poured clarified butter into it, he places [on the fire] three kindling sticks of Aśvattha smeared with clarified butter, each [accompanied] by a verse beginning with 'With kindling the fire...'.
The four officiating priests eat it.
He says: 'Your boiled rice offering for the priests has been prepared!'

4.8.s: saṃvatsaraṃ vā purastāt kuryāt tataḥ sarvān ādadhīta //
4.8.d: संवत्सरं वा पुरस्तात् कुर्यात् ततः सर्वान् आदधीत ॥
4.8.m: Or he should do this a year before; then he should establish all [the fires].

4.8.s: gārhapatye 'nugate grāmāgnim āhṛtya cātuṣprāśyaṃ paktvā viharet //
4.8.d: गार्हपत्ये ऽनुगते ग्रामाग्निम् आहृत्य चातुष्प्राश्यं पक्त्वा विहरेत् ॥
4.8.m: If the Gārhapatya fire goes out, having brought fire from the village and having cooked the mess to be eaten by four [priests], he should distribute the fires.
During the night, [the fire is kept] by staying awake and maintaining it.

4.8.s: vyuṣṭāyām upaśamayya dakṣiṇā vā sam̐hared anvāhāryapacanaś cet //
4.8.d: व्युष्टायाम् उपशमय्य दक्षिणा वा सम्̐हरेद् अन्वाहार्यपचनश् चेत् ॥
4.8.m: At daybreak, having caused [the fire] to go out, or if it is the Anvāhāryapacana fire, he should sweep it away to the south.

4.8.s: sthānam ullikhyābhyukṣyānvārabdhe hiraṇyaṃ nidhāyoṣākhūtkarān nivapaty anteṣu śarkarāḥ //
4.8.d: स्थानम् उल्लिख्याभ्युक्ष्यान्वारब्धे हिरण्यं निधायोषाखूत्करान् निवपत्य् अन्तेषु शर्कराः ॥
4.8.m: Having drawn lines on the site and sprinkled it with water, while [the sacrificer] keeps hold [of him], having laid down gold, he scatters saline soil and earth from molehills, and gravel at the borders.

4.8.s: purastād āhavanīyasyāṣṭāsu prakrameṣv ekādaśasu dvādaśasu matyā vā //
4.8.d: पुरस्ताद् आहवनीयस्याष्टासु प्रक्रमेष्व् एकादशसु द्वादशसु मत्या वा ॥
4.8.m: To the east, for the Āhavanīya fire, at eight, eleven, or twelve paces, or according to judgment.
For the other [hearth, the Dakṣiṇāgni], at one-third [the distance] to the south.
Behind the hearth of the Gārhapatya fire.
Its breathing upon [the fire is accompanied by]: 'I place the breath of life in immortality.'
Its breathing out: 'I place immortality in the breath of life.'

4.9.s: dārubhir jvalantam ādadhāti bhūr bhuvas \\ iti sambhāreṣu \\ amuṣya tvā vratapate vratenādadhe \\ iti yatharṣi //
4.9.d: दारुभिर् ज्वलन्तम् आदधाति भूर् भुवस् \\ इति सम्भारेषु \\ अमुष्य त्वा व्रतपते व्रतेनादधे \\ इति यथर्षि ॥
4.9.m: He sets [the fire] blazing with pieces of wood, upon the sacrificial materials, with 'Bhūr bhuvas...', and with 'By the vow of that lord of vows, so-and-so, I establish you!', according to [his] Ṛṣi.
'By the vow of Varuṇa... [I establish you]' for a Kṣatriya.
'By the vow of Indra... [I establish you]' for a noble.
'By the vow of Manu, the village headman... [I establish you]' for a Vaiśya.
'By the vow of the Ṛbhus... [I establish you]' for a chariot-maker.
He gives the order: 'Sing the Rathantara chant!'
Taking up the carrying vessel with the fuel bundle,
so that the smoke may reach him,
he gives the order: “Sing the Vāmadevya chant.”

4.9.d: अश्वः पुरस्ताद् युवा तदभावे ऽयुवाश्वाभावे ऽनड्वान् ॥
4.9.m: A horse [walks] in front, a young one; in its absence, a non-young one; in the absence of a horse, an ox.

4.9.s: sambhārān adhiṣṭhāpya dakṣiṇapūrvapādena prāñcaṃ nītvāvartya sthāpayati //
4.9.d: सम्भारान् अधिष्ठाप्य दक्षिणपूर्वपादेन प्राञ्चं नीत्वावर्त्य स्थापयति ॥
4.9.m: Having caused [the horse] to step upon the materials with its right front foot, having led it eastward, and having turned it around, he halts it.

4.9.s: agninā pādaṃ dvir upaspṛśya tṛtīyenādadhāti dvitīyena prathamena vā bhūr bhuvaḥ svar iti pūrvavat //
4.9.d: अग्निना पादं द्विर् उपस्पृश्य तृतीयेनादधाति द्वितीयेन प्रथमेन वा भूर् भुवः स्वर् इति पूर्ववत् ॥
4.9.m: Having touched the foot [print] twice with the fire, he establishes [the fire] at the third [touch], or at the second, or at the first, with “bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ”, as before.

4.9.s: purastāt parikramyedhmapūrvārdhaṃ gṛhītvā dyaur iva bhūmnā \\ ity āha //
4.9.d: पुरस्तात् परिक्रम्येध्मपूर्वार्धं गृहीत्वा द्यौर् इव भूम्ना \\ इत्य् आह ॥
4.9.m: Having stepped around to the front and seized the front half of the fuel bundle, he says: “As heaven in abundance…”
And he attends [upon the fire] with the Sārparājñī verses: “This spotted bull…”
From this point on [begins] the maintaining [of the fires] and the attendance upon them.

4.10.m: And he gives the order: “[Sing] the Śyaita, Vāravantīya, and Yajñāyajñīya chants.”
Having gone around the fires to the right, he releases [the horse] towards the north.

Or he may omit the season, the lunar mansion, the materials, the Sāman chants, the shaving, the porridge for the four priests, the keeping vigil, the touching of the front half of the fuel bundle, and the Sārparājñī verses.
And the Agnihotra is offered silently, according to the scriptural text, at the end of the full-spoon oblation.

4.10.s: pūrṇāhutiṃ juhoti nirupyājyaṃ gārhapatye 'dhiśritya sruksruvaṃ ca saṃmṛjyodvāsyotpūyāvekṣya gṛhītvānvārabdha evam̐ sarvatra svāhā \\ iti //
4.10.d: पूर्णाहुतिं जुहोति निरुप्याज्यं गार्हपत्ये ऽधिश्रित्य स्रुक्स्रुवं च संमृज्योद्वास्योत्पूयावेक्ष्य गृहीत्वान्वारब्ध एवम्̐ सर्वत्र स्वाहा \\ इति ॥
4.10.m: He offers the full-spoon oblation, having ladled out the clarified butter, placed it on the Gārhapatya fire, wiped the ladle and dipping spoon, removed [the clarified butter from the fire], purified it, inspected it, and taken it [into the ladle], the sacrificer keeping contact with him, thus everywhere, with “svāhā”.
“I give a boon” is the release of speech.

4.10.s: dvādaśāhānte tanūhavīm̐ṣi nirvapati māse dvitīye tṛtīye ṣaṇmāsye saṃvatsare sadyo vā na vā //
4.10.d: द्वादशाहान्ते तनूहवीम्̐षि निर्वपति मासे द्वितीये तृतीये षण्मास्ये संवत्सरे सद्यो वा न वा ॥
4.10.m: At the end of twelve days he offers the Tanūhavis oblations; or in the second month, the third, the sixth month, after a year, on the same day, or not at all.
The first is to Agni Pavamāna.
The second is to Agni Pāvaka and Agni Śuci.
Or a cake to Agni alone precedes that to Aditi.

4.10.s: ṣaḍ dakṣiṇāḥ prativibhajya dadāti dvādaśa caturvim̐śatiṃ vā //
4.10.d: षड् दक्षिणाः प्रतिविभज्य ददाति द्वादश चतुर्विम्̐शतिं वा ॥
4.10.m: He gives six sacrificial gifts, distributing them [among the priests], or twelve, or twenty-four,
He should avoid falsehood, turning away guests, putting rotten wood on the fire, food cooked in an oven, and water from a boat.

4.10.s: brahmacāry agninityadhārī kṣīrahomy agnim upaśāyī dvādaśarātram̐ ṣaḍrātraṃ trirātram antataḥ //
4.10.d: ब्रह्मचार्य् अग्निनित्यधारी क्षीरहोम्य् अग्निम् उपशायी द्वादशरात्रम्̐ षड्रात्रं त्रिरात्रम् अन्ततः ॥
4.10.m: He must be a student of the Veda, keep the fire continually burning, offer milk as oblation, and sleep near the fire for twelve nights, six nights, or at least three nights.

4.11.m: The re-establishment of the fires belongs to one whose establishment [of the fires] has not turned out successfully,
Having abandoned the fires for at least three nights,
or in the rainy season, at midday.

4.11.s: vrīhyapūpam arkapalāśayoḥ pakvaṃ gārhapatyasthāne nidadhāty evam āhavanīyasya yāvam̐ sadyaś cet //
4.11.d: व्रीह्यपूपम् अर्कपलाशयोः पक्वं गार्हपत्यस्थाने निदधात्य् एवम् आहवनीयस्य यावम्̐ सद्यश् चेत् ॥
4.11.m: He places a cake of rice cooked on leaves of arka and palāśa in the place of the Gārhapatya fire, and likewise [a cake] of barley in that of the Āhavanīya fire, if it is performed on the same day.
A cake on five potsherds is offered to Agni in a low voice before the final after-offering,

4.11.s: agnīn iti vā prathame prayāje 'nuyāje ca //
4.11.d: अग्नीन् इति वा प्रथमे प्रयाजे ऽनुयाजे च ॥
4.11.m: Or he says “agnīn” in the first fore-offering and after-offering.
The second portion of clarified butter is to Agni Pavamāna or to [Agni] Indumat.
Gold is the sacrificial gift, or an ox, or, if he desires, the sacrificial gifts of the establishment of the fires, according to the scriptural text.
The rest is like the establishment of the fires, [performed] in one day.

4.11.s: aparāhṇe maitrāvaruṇī vaśānastamite puroḍāśeḍāntaṃ kṛtvā rātriśṛtayā prātaś caranti tata ādhānam //
4.11.d: अपराह्णे मैत्रावरुणी वशानस्तमिते पुरोडाशेडान्तं कृत्वा रात्रिशृतया प्रातश् चरन्ति तत आधानम् ॥
4.11.m: In the afternoon, a barren cow dedicated to Mitra-Varuṇa [is offered]; before sunset, having carried the rite up to the cake-iḍā, they proceed in the morning with the [meat] cooked through the night; after that [follows] the establishment [of the fires].

4.12.d: सायमाहुत्याम्̐ हुतायां यजमानो ऽग्नी उपतिष्ठते वात्सप्रेण ॥
4.12.m: When the evening oblation has been offered, the sacrificer attends upon the fires with the Vātsapra hymn,

4.12.s: tisras trir upaprayantas \\ asya pratnām \ pari te \ citrāvaso \\ iti ca //
4.12.d: तिस्रस् त्रिर् उपप्रयन्तस् \\ अस्य प्रत्नाम् \ परि ते \ चित्रावसो \\ इति च ॥
4.12.m: Three times with three verses: “Advancing…”, “His ancient…”, “Around thee…”, and with “O Citrāvasu…”
He approaches a cow with: “Ye are food…”
Having gone to the Gārhapatya fire, he attends upon it with: “Unto thee…”
With “The presser of Soma…” [he sips] water, like the taking up of the observance.
The pronouncing of the sons' names is as at the Full-Moon sacrifice.
Or both [attend upon the fires] with “bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ”.
When about to go on a journey, [he attends upon] all [the fires] with “O Narya…”, mantra by mantra.

4.12.s: pravasan yājamānaṃ kuryād yathākālam ātmasaṃskārād dharmamātratvāchruteś ca //
4.12.d: प्रवसन् याजमानं कुर्याद् यथाकालम् आत्मसंस्काराद् धर्ममात्रत्वाछ्रुतेश् च ॥
4.12.m: While residing away, he should perform the sacrificer's duties at the proper times, because they are a personal purification, have the nature of obligatory duty, and because of Vedic text.
And upon returning, restraint of speech [takes place] mentally.

4.12.s: samitpāṇir anupetya kaṃcid upatiṣṭhata āhavanīyagārhapatyadakṣiṇāgnīn āganma \\ iti pratimantram //
4.12.d: समित्पाणिर् अनुपेत्य कंचिद् उपतिष्ठत आहवनीयगार्हपत्यदक्षिणाग्नीन् आगन्म \\ इति प्रतिमन्त्रम् ॥
4.12.m: With fuel stick in hand, without approaching anyone, he attends upon the Āhavanīya, Gārhapatya, and Dakṣiṇāgni fires, with the mantra for each: 'We have come...'
And having sat down, [he attends upon them with] fuel sticks and sweepings-around.
Or the attendance [is done] silently, as before.

4.12.s: gṛhā mā bibhīta \\ iti gṛhān upaiti //
4.12.d: गृहा मा बिभीत \\ इति गृहान् उपैति ॥
4.12.m: he approaches the house with: 'O house, fear not...'
He enters with: 'For security, for you...'
He should not harm the members of the household, if he wishes, [until] tomorrow.

4.13.s: uddhara \\ iti yajamāno brūyāt sāyamprātar agnihotre //
4.13.d: उद्धर \\ इति यजमानो ब्रूयात् सायम्प्रातर् अग्निहोत्रे ॥
4.13.m: The sacrificer should say: 'Take [the fire] up!' at the evening and morning Agnihotra.
The taking up of the Āhavanīya fire from the Gārhapatya fire [takes place] before sunset and before sunrise.

4.13.s: pratyaṅmukho vā sāyaṃ nidadhyāt tasmint sāyamprātar homam eke //
4.13.d: प्रत्यङ्मुखो वा सायं निदध्यात् तस्मिन्त् सायम्प्रातर् होमम् एके ॥
4.13.m: Or, facing west, he may place it down in the evening; some [teachers say that] the offering at evening and morning [takes place] on that [same fire].
In that [fire] they should cook non-meat [food].
In the absence of cooked food, he should tell [them] to place cow's milk over [the fire].
He should tell [them] to make a brāhmaṇa drink it.

4.13.s: antareṇāparāgnī gatvā dakṣiṇena vāpradakṣiṇam āhavanīyaṃ parītyopaviśati yajamānaḥ //
4.13.d: अन्तरेणापराग्नी गत्वा दक्षिणेन वाप्रदक्षिणम् आहवनीयं परीत्योपविशति यजमानः ॥
4.13.m: Going between the two western fires or to the south, having circumambulated the Āhavanīya fire sunwise, the sacrificer sits down.
To the west of the Āhavanīya fire he lays down a grass pad or kuśa grass.

4.13.s: paristaraṇaṃ vā sarveṣāṃ prāgudagbhir udagagrān dakṣiṇāgrān karotīti śruteḥ //
4.13.d: परिस्तरणं वा सर्वेषां प्रागुदग्भिर् उदगग्रान् दक्षिणाग्रान् करोतीति श्रुतेः ॥
4.13.m: Or the strewing [with grass] of all [fires is done] with [grass blades pointing] east and north, because of the Vedic text: 'He makes those pointing north point south.'
Having sprinkled around the Āhavanīya fire, he pours out a continuous stream of water up to the Gārhapatya fire,

4.14.s: agnihotrīṃ dohayati puṃvatsām aśūdreṇa sthālyām āryakṛtyām ūrdhvakapālāyāṃ dakṣiṇataḥ prācīm udīcīṃ vā //
4.14.d: अग्निहोत्रीं दोहयति पुंवत्साम् अशूद्रेण स्थाल्याम् आर्यकृत्याम् ऊर्ध्वकपालायां दक्षिणतः प्राचीम् उदीचीं वा ॥
4.14.m: He has the Agnihotra-cow that has a male calf milked by a non-Śūdra into a pot made by an Ārya, having upward potsherds, to the south, [the cow facing] east or north.

4.14.d: पूर्वेणाहवनीयम् आहृत्य गार्हपत्ये ऽधिश्रयत्य् उत्तरतो निरुह्याङ्गारान् ॥
4.14.m: Having brought [the milk] to the east of the Āhavanīya fire, he places it over the Gārhapatya fire, having raked out burning coals to the north.
In the same manner is the bringing of whatever is meant for the offering in other rites as well.

4.14.s: tṛṇenāvajyotyāsicyāpaḥ punar avajyotya nidhāyaṃ trir udvāsayaty udak //
4.14.d: तृणेनावज्योत्यासिच्यापः पुनर् अवज्योत्य निधायं त्रिर् उद्वासयत्य् उदक् ॥
4.14.m: Having illuminated it with grass, having poured in water, having illuminated it again, having set it down, he takes it off [the fire] three times toward the north.
Having heated the ladle and dipping spoon made of Vikankaṭa wood, he wipes them with his hand.
Having heated [them] again, he says: 'I will ladle out.'
The sacrificer, standing, says: 'Om, ladle out!'
He ladles out four dipping spoonfuls.
He leaves a residue in the pot; a brāhmaṇa should drink it.

4.14.s: upari samidhaṃ dhārayan vārkṣīm adhyadhi gārhapatyād āhavanīyam̐ harati mukhamātre dhārayan //
4.14.d: उपरि समिधं धारयन् वार्क्षीम् अध्यधि गार्हपत्याद् आहवनीयम्̐ हरति मुखमात्रे धारयन् ॥
4.14.m: Holding a wooden fuel stick above, holding it at the height of his mouth, he carries [the ladle] above, from the Gārhapatya fire to the Āhavanīya fire.

4.14.s: madhye nigṛhyodgṛhyopaviśya samidham ādadhāti \\ agnijyotiṣaṃ tvā vāyumatīṃ prāṇavatīm̐ svargyām̐ svargāyopadadhāmi bhāsvatīm iti //
4.14.d: मध्ये निगृह्योद्गृह्योपविश्य समिधम् आदधाति \\ अग्निज्योतिषं त्वा वायुमतीं प्राणवतीम्̐ स्वर्ग्याम्̐ स्वर्गायोपदधामि भास्वतीम् इति ॥
4.14.m: Having lowered it in the middle, having raised it, and having sat down, he places the fuel stick on [the fire] with: 'You, having the light of Agni, accompanied by Vāyu, possessing breath, leading to heaven, I place for heaven, radiant.'

4.14.s: pradīptām abhijuhoti \\ agnir jyotir iti sajūr iti vā //
4.14.d: प्रदीप्ताम् अभिजुहोति \\ अग्निर् ज्योतिर् इति सजूर् इति वा ॥
4.14.m: Upon the blazing [fuel stick] he offers with: 'Agni is light...' or 'United...'
'Agni is splendor...' for one who desires spiritual luster.

4.14.s: kūrce nidhāya gārhapatyam avekṣate hoṣyann asmin //
4.14.d: कूर्चे निधाय गार्हपत्यम् अवेक्षते होष्यन्न् अस्मिन् ॥
4.14.m: Having placed [the ladle] on the grass pad, being about to offer into this [Gārhapatya], he looks at the Gārhapatya fire.
Silently, the second [oblation, which is] larger.
Having shaken it twice, he sets it down.

4.14.s: upamṛjya srucaṃ kūrce nimārṣṭi namo devebhyaḥ //
4.14.d: उपमृज्य स्रुचं कूर्चे निमार्ष्टि नमो देवेभ्यः ॥
4.14.m: Having wiped the ladle, he wipes it downward upon the grass pad with: 'Homage to the gods.'
[He wipes it] to the south, with the hand upward, with: 'Svadhā to the ancestors.'
One who desires prosperity should touch water at both of the other two [fires] as well.

4.14.s: sthālyāḥ sruveṇa \\ iha puṣṭiṃ puṣṭipatir dadhātu \\ iha prajām̐ ramayatu prajāpatiḥ / \ agnaye gṛhapataye rayimate puṣṭipataye svāhā \\ iti gārhapatye //
4.14.d: स्थाल्याः स्रुवेण \\ इह पुष्टिं पुष्टिपतिर् दधातु \\ इह प्रजाम्̐ रमयतु प्रजापतिः । \ अग्नये गृहपतये रयिमते पुष्टिपतये स्वाहा \\ इति गार्हपत्ये ॥
4.14.m: From the pot, with the dipping spoon, [he offers] in the Gārhapatya fire with: 'Here let the lord of prosperity bestow prosperity; here let Prajāpati delight the offspring! To Agni, lord of the house, wealthy, lord of prosperity, svāhā!'

4.14.s: agnaye 'nnādāyānnapataye svāhā \\ iti dakṣiṇāgnau tūṣṇīṃ dvitīyām //
4.14.d: अग्नये ऽन्नादायान्नपतये स्वाहा \\ इति दक्षिणाग्नौ तूष्णीं द्वितीयाम् ॥
4.14.m: In the Dakṣiṇāgni fire [he offers] with: 'To Agni, eater of food, lord of food, svāhā!'; silently, the second [oblation].
He eats twice with the ring finger.

4.14.s: utsṛpya nirleḍhyācamyotsiñcati devān jinva \ pitṝn jinva tṛtīyām udukṣati saptaṛṣīn jinva \\ iti //
4.14.d: उत्सृप्य निर्लेढ्याचम्योत्सिञ्चति देवान् जिन्व \ पितॄन् जिन्व तृतीयाम् उदुक्षति सप्तऋषीन् जिन्व \\ इति ॥
4.14.m: Having crept out, having licked [the spoon], and having sipped water, he pours out [water] with: 'Delight the gods!', 'Delight the ancestors!'; for the third [time] he sprinkles water upward with: 'Delight the Seven Sages!'

4.14.s: caturthī kūrcasthāne trir niṣiñcati \\ agnaye pṛthivīkṣite svāhā \ pṛthivyā amṛtaṃ juhomi svāhā \\ amṛte 'mṛtaṃ juhomi svāhā \\ iti //
4.14.d: चतुर्थी कूर्चस्थाने त्रिर् निषिञ्चति \\ अग्नये पृथिवीक्षिते स्वाहा \ पृथिव्या अमृतं जुहोमि स्वाहा \\ अमृते ऽमृतं जुहोमि स्वाहा \\ इति ॥
4.14.m: With the fourth [action], he pours down three times on the place of the grass pad with: 'To Agni, who dwells on earth, svāhā! I offer immortality from the earth, svāhā! I offer immortality into immortality, svāhā!'
Having heated the ladle and dipping spoon in the Āhavanīya fire, he sets them down.

4.14.s: samidha ādadhāti sarveṣu yathāparyukṣitamm \\ samid asi \ samiddho me 'gne dīdihi \ samedhā te agne dīdyāsām iti //
4.14.d: समिध आदधाति सर्वेषु यथापर्युक्षितम्म् \\ समिद् असि \ समिद्धो मे ऽग्ने दीदिहि \ समेधा ते अग्ने दीद्यासाम् इति ॥
4.14.m: He places fuel sticks on all [fires] in the order in which they were sprinkled around, with: 'A fuel stick you are; kindled for me, shine, O Agni; may I shine with your kindling, O Agni.'
Restraining his speech from the milking onwards until the offering, if he is one who offers milk.

4.15.s: antareṇāparāgnī gatvā dakṣiṇena vā pradakṣiṇaṃ gārhapatyaṃ parītyopaviśati yajamānaḥ //
4.15.d: अन्तरेणापराग्नी गत्वा दक्षिणेन वा प्रदक्षिणं गार्हपत्यं परीत्योपविशति यजमानः ॥
4.15.m: Having gone between the western fires or to the south, circumambulating the Gārhapatya fire from left to right, the sacrificer sits down.

4.15.s: apa ācāmati vṛṣṭir asi \ vṛśca me pāpmānam \\ satyena vratam upaimi \\ āpaḥ satyaṃ mayi vratam iti //
4.15.d: अप आचामति वृष्टिर् असि \ वृश्च मे पाप्मानम् \\ सत्येन व्रतम् उपैमि \\ आपः सत्यं मयि व्रतम् इति ॥
4.15.m: He sips water with: "You are rain; cut off my evil. With truth I enter upon the vow. Water is truth; in me is the vow."

4.15.s: vācaṃ visṛjya punar ācāmati vidyud asi \ vi me pāpmānaṃ jahi \\ apo 'vabhṛtham abhyupaimi \ mayi satyaṃ goṣu me vratam iti //
4.15.d: वाचं विसृज्य पुनर् आचामति विद्युद् असि \ वि मे पाप्मानं जहि \\ अपो ऽवभृथम् अभ्युपैमि \ मयि सत्यं गोषु मे व्रतम् इति ॥
4.15.m: Releasing his speech, he sips water again with: "You are lightning; strike away my evil. I approach the waters, the purificatory bath. In me is truth, in my cows is the vow."
"I bring forward [the offering]," he says in the morning.
The placing of the kindling stick, the sprinkling around, and the continuous stream [of water] end towards the east.
Or in the morning [he recites]: "Sūrya is light..."
For one who desires heaven, [he offers] just when [the sun] has set, and at sunrise [in the morning].

4.15.s: tamo 'bhyaye sāyaṃ juhuyād viyati prātar āyuṣkāmasya //
4.15.d: तमो ऽभ्यये सायं जुहुयाद् वियति प्रातर् आयुष्कामस्य ॥
4.15.m: For one who desires a full life, he should offer in the evening when darkness has arrived, and in the morning when [the sky] is clear.
For one who desires cattle, evening and morning [when the cattle are] inside [the pen].
For one who desires prosperity, in the morning while [the cattle are] lying down.

4.15.s: prathamasamiddhe dhūpyamāne prajāsu nihatyeva sahasānnam atsyataḥ //
4.15.d: प्रथमसमिद्धे धूप्यमाने प्रजासु निहत्येव सहसान्नम् अत्स्यतः ॥
4.15.m: When [the fire] is first kindled and smoking, for one who intends to eat food suddenly, as if striking down among the creatures.
When the flame is abundant, [for one who intends to eat food] suddenly, as if seizing [it].
When it is most blazed up, for one who desires prosperity and fame.
When the flame has diminished, for one who intends to eat food through friendship.
When the embers are glowing brightly, for one who desires spiritual luster.
One who desires heaven or one who desires cattle [offers] with milk.
And [for curd] there is no heating over the fire, on account of revealed text and practical capacity.
He should offer for a year with each one of these in connection with a specific desire.
The entrance is by the south in the Agnihotra and the seasonal sacrifices.
In the evening and morning [there is] sitting by and attending upon the Āhavanīya fire.
Or lying down and sitting near the Gārhapatya fire.
While walking, he recollects the Dakṣiṇāgni fire in his mind.
Without having eaten, for a muhūrta in the morning, [there is] sitting in the hall near the Sabhya fire.

5.1.m: The performance of the Four-Month sacrifices [begins] on the full-moon day of Phālguna.
If he wishes, after having offered to Vaiśvānara and Parjanya.
The [cake] for Vaiśvānara is on twelve potsherds.
[A cake] for Savitṛ on twelve potsherds or on eight potsherds.
A caru of coarsely ground grains for Pūṣan.
Even when [offered to] two deities, by virtue of the mandatory rule.
Or half-ground, by virtue of the capacity of both.
And because of the observation [of the text] regarding the offering to Soma and Pūṣan.
Or unground, because of the difference of deity.
[A cake] on seven potsherds for the Maruts possessed of inherent power.
[A cake] on one potsherd for Dyāvāpṛthivī.
The same [garments are worn] also in the Varuṇapraghāsa rites.
Having tied the sacrificial grass in three bundles, [he ties them] again into one.
The prastara bundle is tied up [with it], having shoots of Kuśa grass.

5.1.s: agner janitram iti śakalam ādāya vedyāṃ karoti //
5.1.d: अग्नेर् जनित्रम् इति शकलम् आदाय वेद्यां करोति ॥
5.1.m: Taking a wood chip with the words, "The birthplace of Agni," he places it on the altar.
With the words, "You two are the testicles," [he places] two young blades of Kuśa upon it.
With the words, "You are Urvaśī," [he places] the lower churning stick upon the two [blades].

5.1.s: āyur asi \\ ity uttarayājyasthālīṃ sam̐spṛśya purūravās \\ ity abhinidhānaṃ tayā //
5.1.d: आयुर् असि \\ इत्य् उत्तरयाज्यस्थालीं सम्̐स्पृश्य पुरूरवास् \\ इत्य् अभिनिधानं तया ॥
5.1.m: With the words, "You are Āyus," having touched the clarified-butter pot with the upper [churning stick], with the words, "[You are] Purūravas," [he makes] the placing upon [the lower stick] with it.

5.2.m: He causes [the Hotṛ] to recite for Agni being churned.

5.2.s: manthati gāyatreṇa \\ iti pratimantraṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇam //
5.2.d: मन्थति गायत्रेण \\ इति प्रतिमन्त्रं त्रिः प्रदक्षिणम् ॥
5.2.m: He churns three times clockwise, with each mantra: "With the Gāyatra [metre]..."
When about to throw [it into the fire, he causes him to recite] with the words: "For [Agni] being carried forward..."
With the words, "Be for us...," he throws it [into the Āhavanīya].

5.2.s: agnāv agnir iti juhoti sthālyāḥ sruveṇa //
5.2.d: अग्नाव् अग्निर् इति जुहोति स्थाल्याः स्रुवेण ॥
5.2.m: With the words, "Agni in Agni," he makes an oblation from the pot with the dipping spoon.
[There are] nine fore-offerings and nine after-offerings.
[This applies to] the Varuṇapraghāsa rites and the Mahāhavis rite.

5.2.s: trīṇi samiṣṭayajūm̐ṣi juhoti devā gātuvidas \\ yajña yajñam \ eṣa te \\ iti //
5.2.d: त्रीणि समिष्टयजूम्̐षि जुहोति देवा गातुविदस् \\ यज्ञ यज्ञम् \ एष ते \\ इति ॥
5.2.m: He offers three samiṣṭayajus oblations with the words: "O gods, finders of the path...," "O sacrifice, to the sacrifice...," and "This is yours..."
At the conclusion of each seasonal sacrifice (parvan), or before the last one, shaving [takes place].

5.2.s: apareṇa dakṣiṇāgniṃ dakṣiṇaṃ godānam undati savitrā prasūtā daivyā āpa undantu te tanūṃ dīrghāyutvāya varcase \\ iti //
5.2.d: अपरेण दक्षिणाग्निं दक्षिणं गोदानम् उन्दति सवित्रा प्रसूता दैव्या आप उन्दन्तु ते तनूं दीर्घायुत्वाय वर्चसे \\ इति ॥
5.2.m: To the west of the Dakṣiṇa fire, he moistens the right side of the head with the words: "Impelled by Savitṛ, may the divine waters moisten your body for long life, for splendor."

5.2.s: tryeṇyā śalalyā vinīya trīṇi kuśataruṇāny antardadhāti \\ oṣadhe \\ iti //
5.2.d: त्र्येण्या शलल्या विनीय त्रीणि कुशतरुणान्य् अन्तर्दधाति \\ ओषधे \\ इति ॥
5.2.m: Having parted [the hair] with a three-striped porcupine quill, he inserts three young Kuśa shoots with the words: "O plant..."

5.2.s: śivo nāma \\ iti lohakṣuram ādāya nivartayāmi \\ iti vapati //
5.2.d: शिवो नाम \\ इति लोहक्षुरम् आदाय निवर्तयामि \\ इति वपति ॥
5.2.m: Taking an iron razor with the words, "Auspicious by name," he shaves with the words, "I turn away..."
In the same way, at the back and on the north side.
The Full-Moon sacrifice [takes place] at home, with [the fires] taken up into [the churning sticks] and churned out, if it happens to be thus.
Also for one desirous of offspring, the Vaiśvadeva rite [is performed].

5.2.s: eke 'dhaḥprāṅśāyī madhvāśy ṛtujāyopāyī mām̐sastryanṛtāni varjayed udakābhyavāyaṃ ca prāg avabhṛthāt //
5.2.d: एके ऽधःप्राङ्शायी मध्वाश्य् ऋतुजायोपायी माम्̐सस्त्र्यनृतानि वर्जयेद् उदकाभ्यवायं च प्राग् अवभृथात् ॥
5.2.m: Some [prescribe]: He should sleep on the ground facing eastward, eat honey, approach his wife [only] in her fertile period, abstain from meat, women, and falsehood, and avoid bathing in water until the concluding bath (avabhṛtha).

5.3.s: āṣāḍhām ayaṃ te yonir iti samārohyodavasāya nirmathya varuṇapraghāsāḥ //
5.3.d: आषाढाम् अयं ते योनिर् इति समारोह्योदवसाय निर्मथ्य वरुणप्रघासाः ॥
5.3.m: At the Āṣāḍhī [full moon], having mounted [the fires] with the words, "This is your birthplace," having departed [to the sacrificial place] and churned out [the fires], the Varuṇapraghāsa rites [are performed].
On the previous day, on the Dakṣiṇa fire, the making of dough-vessels (karambhapātra) from unhusked, unroasted barley [takes place].
As many as are the household members of the sacrificer, with one added.
Or [as many] as are his offspring, because of the Vedic text speaking of "born".
Having washed wool that does not come from a sheep, he should stick it onto the two.
To the east of the Āhavanīya, he makes two altars.

5.3.s: caturaratnir vā paścāt sapta prācī ṣaḍ vā trayaḥ purastāt //
5.3.d: चतुररत्निर् वा पश्चात् सप्त प्राची षड् वा त्रयः पुरस्तात् ॥
5.3.m: Or four cubits at the back, seven cubits eastward, or six, and three cubits in front.
Beginning with the wooden sword, he performs [the rites] up to the touching [of the altar].
The passage of the Pratiprasthātṛ priest is to the west of the altar.
He throws up the high altar (uttaravedi) on the northern [altar].

5.3.s: śamyām ādāya cātvālaṃ mimīte pūrveṇotkaram̐ saṃcaraṃ parihāpya //
5.3.d: शम्याम् आदाय चात्वालं मिमीते पूर्वेणोत्करम्̐ संचरं परिहाप्य ॥
5.3.m: Taking the yoke-pin (śamyā), he measures out the Cātvāla pit to the east of the rubbish heap, leaving room for the passage.
He places the yoke-pin pointing northward [on the west].
With the wooden sword he delineates inside with each mantra: "O Taptāyanī..."

5.3.s: vided agnir iti cātvāle praharati sphyenānvārabdhe //
5.3.d: विदेद् अग्निर् इति चात्वाले प्रहरति स्फ्येनान्वारब्धे ॥
5.3.m: With the words, "Agni has found...," he strikes into the Cātvāla pit, which is touched by the wooden sword.

5.3.s: agne aṅgiras \\ iti purīṣam̐ harati hastena ca //
5.3.d: अग्ने अङ्गिरस् \\ इति पुरीषम्̐ हरति हस्तेन च ॥
5.3.m: With the words, "O Agni, Aṅgiras...," he carries the loose earth, also with his hand.

5.3.d: यो ऽस्याम् इति निवपति पूर्वार्धे शङ्कुसहितम् ॥
5.3.m: With the words, "Who on this...," he pours it out on the eastern half, together with the peg.
The Agnīdh priest [takes earth] silently, like the rubbish heap, when it is carried.
The difference is: "In the second...", "In the third..."

5.3.s: anu tvā \\ iti caturthaṃ yathārtham āhṛtya sim̐hy asi \\ iti vyūhaty uttaravedim̐ śamyāmātrīm //
5.3.d: अनु त्वा \\ इति चतुर्थं यथार्थम् आहृत्य सिम्̐ह्य् असि \\ इति व्यूहत्य् उत्तरवेदिम्̐ शम्यामात्रीम् ॥
5.3.m: Having fetched [earth] for the fourth time according to need with [the mantra], 'After you...', he spreads out the high altar (uttaravedi), measuring one śamyā, with [the mantra], 'You are a lioness...'.
Or [it measures] one third [of the vedi], or is unmeasured, or measures a yoke, or [is measured] by ten steps of the sacrificer.
Or [these larger dimensions belong] in the Soma sacrifice, because of the scripture mentioning the high altar being the latter, or because of [the text stating] 'vyapasphuraṇa' (spreading out).
In the center, he makes a navel (nābhi) measuring a span, four-cornered.

5.3.s: prokṣaty uttaravedim̐ sikatāś ca prakirati sim̐hy asi \\ iti pratimantram //
5.3.d: प्रोक्षत्य् उत्तरवेदिम्̐ सिकताश् च प्रकिरति सिम्̐ह्य् असि \\ इति प्रतिमन्त्रम् ॥
5.3.m: He sprinkles the high altar and scatters sand with the respective mantra, 'You are a lioness...'.

5.4.m: In the morning, having taken five ladlings [of clarified butter], he brings forward the two fires, having supported them with two fuel bundles.
Or [he brings forward] everything, dividing it, because of [its rule in] the archetype rite.
Or the bringing forward is from the Soma sacrifice, because it must be stated [separately here].
The taking [of the five ladlings] is for a supplementary purpose, because of the placing of the fire on the high altar.

5.4.s: ājyaprokṣaṇīr udyamyāgnī cāha \\ agnibhyāṃ prahriyamāṇābhyām anubrūhi \\ ekasphyayānūdehi \\ iti //
5.4.d: आज्यप्रोक्षणीर् उद्यम्याग्नी चाह \\ अग्निभ्यां प्रह्रियमाणाभ्याम् अनुब्रूहि \\ एकस्फ्ययानूदेहि \\ इति ॥
5.4.m: Having lifted up the clarified butter and the sprinkling waters, and the two fires, he says: 'Recite for the two fires being carried forward; follow along with a single wooden sword.'
When [the verse] has been recited three times, the carrying forward [takes place] according to the vedi.
The Pratiprasthātṛ draws a line with the wooden sword as far as the hip of the vedi.

5.4.s: vedyantare sthitvodaṅṅ uttaravediṃ prokṣati \\ indraghoṣas \\ iti pratimantraṃ pratidiśaṃ yathāliṅgam //
5.4.d: वेद्यन्तरे स्थित्वोदङ्ङ् उत्तरवेदिं प्रोक्षति \\ इन्द्रघोषस् \\ इति प्रतिमन्त्रं प्रतिदिशं यथालिङ्गम् ॥
5.4.m: Standing between the two vedis and facing north, he sprinkles the high altar with the respective mantra towards each quarter according to the mark: 'Indraghoṣa...'.

5.4.s: dakṣiṇām̐sasahitaṃ bahirvedi śeṣaṃ niṣiñcati \\ idam ahaṃ taptaṃ vār iti //
5.4.d: दक्षिणाम्̐ससहितं बहिर्वेदि शेषं निषिञ्चति \\ इदम् अहं तप्तं वार् इति ॥
5.4.m: Along with the southern shoulder, he pours out the remainder outside the vedi with: 'This warm water, I...'.

5.4.s: nābhyāḥ śroṇyam̐seṣu pañcagṛhītaṃ juhoty akṣṇayā dakṣiṇe 'm̐se śroṇyām̐ śroṇyām am̐se madhye ca hiraṇyaṃ paśyant sim̐hy asi \\ iti pratimantram //
5.4.d: नाभ्याः श्रोण्यम्̐सेषु पञ्चगृहीतं जुहोत्य् अक्ष्णया दक्षिणे ऽम्̐से श्रोण्याम्̐ श्रोण्याम् अम्̐से मध्ये च हिरण्यं पश्यन्त् सिम्̐ह्य् असि \\ इति प्रतिमन्त्रम् ॥
5.4.m: At the hips and shoulders of the navel, he offers the five ladlings diagonally—at the southern shoulder, at the hip, at the [other] hip, at the [other] shoulder, and in the middle—looking at a piece of gold, with the respective mantra, 'You are a lioness...'.
He lifts up the ladle with: 'For the beings, you...'.

5.4.s: nābhiṃ paitudāravaiḥ paridadhāti pūrvavad dhruvo 'si \\ iti pratimantram //
5.4.d: नाभिं पैतुदारवैः परिदधाति पूर्ववद् ध्रुवो ऽसि \\ इति प्रतिमन्त्रम् ॥
5.4.m: He encloses the navel with sticks of paitudārava wood as before, with the respective mantra, 'You are steadfast...'.

5.4.s: agneḥ purīṣam iti nivapati gulgulusugandhitejanavṛṣṇestukāś copari śīrṣaṇyā abhāve 'nyāḥ //
5.4.d: अग्नेः पुरीषम् इति निवपति गुल्गुलुसुगन्धितेजनवृष्णेस्तुकाश् चोपरि शीर्षण्या अभावे ऽन्याः ॥
5.4.m: He scatters [scented earth] with 'Agni's rubble...', and above [it] bdellium, sugandhitejana grass, and tufts of ram's wool from the head, or others if these are lacking.
On the raised and sprinkled [ground], [he deposits] the southern [fire].
He strews down the supporting [embers/fuel].
Or the taking up of the vow [is done now], if it was not done [earlier].

5.4.s: nityebhyo 'dhikāny aindrāgnaḥ payasye vāruṇīṃ mārutī kāya ekakapālaḥ //
5.4.d: नित्येभ्यो ऽधिकान्य् ऐन्द्राग्नः पयस्ये वारुणीं मारुती काय एककपालः ॥
5.4.m: Additional to the regular [offerings] are: the cake for Indra and Agni, the two curds (payasyā)—the Vāruṇī and the Mārutī—and the one-pot-sherd cake for Ka.
The southern [set belongs] to the Pratiprasthātṛ.

5.4.s: dhruvāyāḥ purastāt pṛṣadājyam ājyaṃ dadhimiśraṃ pañcagṛhītam \\ jyotir asi \\ iti samidantena //
5.4.d: ध्रुवायाः पुरस्तात् पृषदाज्यम् आज्यं दधिमिश्रं पञ्चगृहीतम् \\ ज्योतिर् असि \\ इति समिदन्तेन ॥
5.4.m: In front of the Dhruvā ladle, [he takes] five ladlings of speckled butter—clarified butter mixed with curd—ending with the kindling-stick mantra, with: 'You are light...'.
[This is] for the after-offerings everywhere.
Or [it is placed down] with 'With your beloved seat...', because of the non-specific teaching.
Or [the speckled butter is taken] later, because of its later time [of use].

The Pratiprasthātṛ does not perform the praṇītā water, girding of the wife, churning of fire, calling and answering, giving directions, having the sacrificer recite, seating and choosing of the Hotṛ, finger-joint anointing of the Prāśitra, the intermediate Iḍā portion, the posterior fire rites, or the preparatory bath.
Elsewhere he imitates what has been done [by the Adhvaryu], on the southern [altar].

5.5.m: Having poured out the whey, he scatters into both [curds] karīra fruits mixed with leaves of śamī and palāśa.
He places all the sacrificial offerings on the northern [altar].
The Pratiprasthātṛ [places] the Mārutī [curds] along with its clarified butter on the southern [altar].

5.5.s: saṃmārjanāya preṣite 'saṃmṛṣṭe pratiprasthātā patnīm āneṣyann āha kena carasi \\ iti //
5.5.d: संमार्जनाय प्रेषिते ऽसंमृष्टे प्रतिप्रस्थाता पत्नीम् आनेष्यन्न् आह केन चरसि \\ इति ॥
5.5.m: When the order for sweeping [the fire] has been given, but before it is swept, the Pratiprasthātṛ, about to lead up the wife, says: 'With whom do you consort?'
Or she raises stalks of grass, one for each paramour.
Because of the scripture: 'What is not declared brings harm to the kinsmen.'

5.5.s: ākhyāte praghāsinas \\ ity enāṃ vācayati nayan //
5.5.d: आख्याते प्रघासिनस् \\ इत्य् एनां वाचयति नयन् ॥
5.5.m: When they have been declared, while leading her he causes her to recite: 'O ravenous ones...'.

5.5.s: karambhapātrāṇi juhoti śūrpeṇa mūrdhani kṛtvā dakṣiṇe 'gnau pratyaṅmukhī jāyāpatī vā dakṣiṇenāhṛtya tīrthena pūrveṇa vedim apareṇa vā yad grāme \\ iti //
5.5.d: करम्भपात्राणि जुहोति शूर्पेण मूर्धनि कृत्वा दक्षिणे ऽग्नौ प्रत्यङ्मुखी जायापती वा दक्षिणेनाहृत्य तीर्थेन पूर्वेण वेदिम् अपरेण वा यद् ग्रामे \\ इति ॥
5.5.m: Having placed the groat-vessels on her head by means of a winnowing basket, facing west at the southern fire, she offers them, or both wife and husband offer, having fetched them by the southern [path], either by the passage east of the vedi or west [of it], with: 'Whatever [sin] in the village...'.

5.5.s: mo ṣū ṇas \\ iti yajamāno japati //
5.5.d: मो षू णस् \\ इति यजमानो जपति ॥
5.5.m: The sacrificer mutters: 'Do not indeed to us...'.

5.5.s: akran karma \\ ity enāṃ vācayati pratinayan //
5.5.d: अक्रन् कर्म \\ इत्य् एनां वाचयति प्रतिनयन् ॥
5.5.m: Leading her back, he causes her to recite: 'They have performed the rite...'.
When she has returned, [the ritual proceeds] from the sweeping [of the fire] up to the two butter portions.
The Pratiprasthātṛ sits with ladle in hand.
At the time of proceeding with the curd offering (payasyā), the two [priests] exchange the two sheep.
[Each offers] the sheep together with either of the cuttings.

5.5.s: savyena srucau gṛhītvā pratiprasthātur vāso dakṣiṇena marudbhyo 'nuvācayati //
5.5.d: सव्येन स्रुचौ गृहीत्वा प्रतिप्रस्थातुर् वासो दक्षिणेन मरुद्भ्यो ऽनुवाचयति ॥
5.5.m: Having taken the two ladles with the left hand, and the Pratiprasthātṛ's garment with the right, he causes [the Hotṛ] to recite the invitatory verse for the Maruts.
When the oblations have been performed, both [proceed] from the Sviṣṭakṛt offering onward.
Having cut off [portions for] the iḍā, he hands [the vessel] to the Pratiprasthātṛ.
There the Pratiprasthātṛ [cuts off portions] of [the cake] for the Maruts.
Pouring together [the whey, there is] consumption of the vājina.
The Pratiprasthātṛ [takes part] in the consumptions, because he is an alteration of the Adhvaryu;
and the Maitrāvaruṇa, because he is an alteration of the Hotṛ and Adhvaryu.
[He offers] the samiṣṭayajus formulas silently in the southern [fire].
The final purificatory bath is performed with the scrapings of [the curd offered] to Varuṇa.
Going silently [to water] and entering it, he submerges it with: “O purificatory bath...”
Wife and husband bathe without submerging [their heads].
They rub each other's back.
They put on other clothes.
He should give the previous [clothes] to the officiating priests, [or] to whomever he wishes.

5.5.s: yathetam etyāhavanīye samidādhānam \\ devānām̐ samid asi \\ iti //
5.5.d: यथेतम् एत्याहवनीये समिदाधानम् \\ देवानाम्̐ समिद् असि \\ इति ॥
5.5.m: Having returned by the path they came, the laying on of a fuel stick on the Āhavanīya [takes place] with: “You are the fuel stick of the gods...”
And the wife [lays a stick] on the Gārhapatya silently.

5.6.m: On the full moon of Kārttika, the Sākamedha [offerings take place over] two days.
On the previous day, in the forenoon, there is a cake for Agni Anīkavant.
At midday, a caru for the Maruts Sāṃtapanas.
It concludes with the samiṣṭayajus formulas;
or with the exclusion of throwing the sacrificial grass [into the fire].

5.6.s: idhmasthāne śakalaparidhi nidhāya marudbhyo gṛhamedhibhyaḥ sāyaṃ caruḥ payasi //
5.6.d: इध्मस्थाने शकलपरिधि निधाय मरुद्भ्यो गृहमेधिभ्यः सायं चरुः पयसि ॥
5.6.m: In place of the fuel bundle, having deposited enclosing sticks of wood-chips, in the evening there is a caru in milk for the Maruts Gṛhamedhins.
Having cooked [the caru], basted it, and taken it off [the fire], he ladles it out into two platters,

5.6.s: āsecane madhye kṛtvā sarpir āsiñcaty ājyārtham //
5.6.d: आसेचने मध्ये कृत्वा सर्पिर् आसिञ्चत्य् आज्यार्थम् ॥
5.6.m: Having made an indentation in the middle, he pours in melted butter for the sake of ghee.

5.6.s: staraṇayajuṣā vedim abhimṛśya tūṣṇīṃ vā kṛtatvāt paridhiparidhānam //
5.6.d: स्तरणयजुषा वेदिम् अभिमृश्य तूष्णीं वा कृतत्वात् परिधिपरिधानम् ॥
5.6.m: Having touched the altar with the strewing formula, or silently because it is already done, the laying of the enclosing sticks [is performed].
Having put on the wood-chips, he sets down the two [platters] ladled out according to his discretion.
And he wipes the ladle and the dipping spoon;
or the wiping [is done] without taking [the caru] off [the fire].
He performs [the offerings of] the two portions of ghee:
And the Gṛhamedha [caru] and Sviṣṭakṛt offerings, like the portions of ghee, have cuttings taken equally,
and without rebasting.
he sets on the fire ghee along with [the caru].
Taking both off [the fire], he sets them down.
After invoking [the iḍā], cleansing [takes place] first.

5.6.s: yajamānagṛhyā haviruchiṣṭāśā ṛtvijo brāhmaṇāś cānye bahuścet //
5.6.d: यजमानगृह्या हविरुछिष्टाशा ऋत्विजो ब्राह्मणाश् चान्ये बहुश्चेत् ॥
5.6.m: The members of the sacrificer's household eat the remnant of the sacrificial substance, [and so do] the officiating priests and other Brahmins, if there are many.
He sets down the pot not empty,
having completed the offering to the Sāṃtapanas;
Having united the calves with their mothers, he ties up the calf of a cow suckling another's calf.
The Agnihotra offering is made of barley gruel.

5.6.s: prātar hutvāhutvā vā sthālyāṃ darvyādatte pūrṇā darvi \\ iti //
5.6.d: प्रातर् हुत्वाहुत्वा वा स्थाल्यां दर्व्यादत्ते पूर्णा दर्वि \\ इति ॥
5.6.m: In the morning, whether having offered [the Agnihotra] or not having offered, he takes [a portion] with a ladle from the pot with: “Full ladle...”
He should order [someone] to call a bull.
If it does not utter a sound, the Brahman says: “Make the offering!”

5.7.m: A cake on seven potsherds is for the sporting Maruts.
Or they share the same sacrificial grass, because their time and ritual actions are identical.
Having concluded the Udavasānīyā rite and churned out fire, one performs the Mahāhavis.
a cake on one potsherd for Viśvakarman.
The high altar, the bringing forward of the fire, the churning, and the speckled clarified butter are as in the Varuṇapraghāsa rite.

5.8.m: In the Pitṛyajña, the performance is in a low voice.
The Dakṣiṇāgni fire functions like the Āhavanīya fire.
He carries the praṇītā waters past by the east of the Āhavanīya fire.
A cake on six potsherds is for the Fathers accompanied by Soma.
Parched grains are for the Fathers seated on the sacrificial grass.
A gruel drink is for the Agniṣvātta Fathers.
The pounding and the grinding take place to the east of the Gārhapatya fire.
The setting down of the potsherds is on the southern half.
The roasting of the parched grains is on the Dakṣiṇāgni fire.
Even when the order of cooking and grinding is inverted, the prescribed rules apply.

5.8.s: abhimṛśyārdhāḥ piṣṭvā nivānyādugdhe sakṛnmathita ekaśalākayā manthaḥ //
5.8.d: अभिमृश्यार्धाः पिष्ट्वा निवान्यादुग्धे सकृन्मथित एकशलाकया मन्थः ॥
5.8.m: Having touched [the roasted grains], he grinds half of them; stirred once into the milk of a cow that has lost her calf using a single twig, it becomes the gruel drink.

5.8.d: अग्रहणं मन्थस्य ततो ऽर्धाः पिम्̐षन्तीति श्रुतेः ॥
5.8.m: There is no separate scooping for the gruel drink, because the scripture says: 'From that they grind half'.
Or there is a scooping, because it is specifically enjoined.

5.8.s: dakṣiṇena dakṣiṇāgniṃ parivṛtam udagdvāraṃ tanmadhye vediṃ karoty avāntaradiksraktim āptyānte //
5.8.d: दक्षिणेन दक्षिणाग्निं परिवृतम् उदग्द्वारं तन्मध्ये वेदिं करोत्य् अवान्तरदिक्स्रक्तिम् आप्त्यान्ते ॥
5.8.m: To the south of the Dakṣiṇāgni fire, in an enclosed space with its entrance to the north, he makes an altar in the middle, its corners pointing toward the intermediate directions, ending at the water-vessels.
He establishes the Dakṣiṇāgni fire in its middle.
And the Brahman and the sacrificer follow along.
Wearing the sacred thread over the left shoulder, he scoops the clarified butter.

5.8.s: visram̐sya yūnaṃ cāgre gṛhītvā tri stṛṇann agniṃ paryeti //
5.8.d: विस्रम्̐स्य यूनं चाग्रे गृहीत्वा त्रि स्तृणन्न् अग्निं पर्येति ॥
5.8.m: Having untied it, taking hold of both the band and the tip, spreading it three times, he goes around the fire.
Leaving only enough for the prastara-bundle, he goes around in the reverse direction by that amount.
The setting down of the sacrificial substances ends toward the east.
From the prompting for the kindling verses up to the two portions of clarified butter, all wear the sacred thread over the left shoulder.
The Brahman and the sacrificer go around behind.

5.8.s: āśrāvya sīda hotar ity eva brūyāt //
5.8.d: आश्राव्य सीद होतर् इत्य् एव ब्रूयात् ॥
5.8.m: Having called for the response, he should say simply: 'Be seated, Hotṛ priest!'
Or there is no bringing together [of the ladles], because of the connection with the sacrificial grass.

5.9.m: About to proceed with the sacrificial substances, they turn back in reverse.

5.9.d: सर्वेभ्यो ऽवद्यति यथापूर्वम्̐ सोमवद्भ्यो मध्यात् सकृत्सकृत् ॥
5.9.m: He cuts portions from all of them in order: for the Fathers accompanied by Soma, from the middle, once from each.
In this way, for the Fathers seated on the sacrificial grass, [he cuts portions] from the north, of parched grains, gruel drink, and cake.
For the Agniṣvātta Fathers, [he cuts portions] from the south, of gruel drink, cake, and parched grains.
[He cuts portions] in the front for Agni Kavyavāhana as previously.

5.9.s: om̐ svadhā \\ iti \\ astu svadhā \\ iti vāśrutapratyāśrute //
5.9.d: ओम्̐ स्वधा \\ इति \\ अस्तु स्वधा \\ इति वाश्रुतप्रत्याश्रुते ॥
5.9.m: "Om svadhā!" or "Astu svadhā!" are the call and the response.
"Svadhā namaḥ" is the vaṣaṭ-call.

5.9.s: mantham upahūya hotādhvaryur brahmāgnīd avaghrāyaṃ nidadhati //
5.9.d: मन्थम् उपहूय होताध्वर्युर् ब्रह्माग्नीद् अवघ्रायं निदधति ॥
5.9.m: Having invoked the stirred drink, the Hotṛ, the Adhvaryu, the Brahman, and the Agnīdh lay it down after having smelled it,
having cut off the Prāśitra portion or the Iḍā;

5.9.s: vediṃ triḥ pariṣiñcaty udapātreṇādhvaryur yajamāno vā //
5.9.d: वेदिं त्रिः परिषिञ्चत्य् उदपात्रेणाध्वर्युर् यजमानो वा ॥
5.9.m: The Adhvaryu or the sacrificer sprinkles water around the vedi three times with a vessel of water.
At the corners, having sprinkled water each time for the washing of the Fathers as previously,
first at the north-western [corner],

5.9.s: savye samavadāya sarvebhyo yathāvaniktaṃ piṇḍān dadāti \\ asāv etat te \\ iti //
5.9.d: सव्ये समवदाय सर्वेभ्यो यथावनिक्तं पिण्डान् ददाति \\ असाव् एतत् ते \\ इति ॥
5.9.m: having gathered [portions] from all in his left hand, he gives rice balls according to the washing: "N.N., this is yours!"

5.9.s: uttarapūrvasyāṃ pāṇī nimṛṣṭe \\ atra pitaras \\ iti //
5.9.d: उत्तरपूर्वस्यां पाणी निमृष्टे \\ अत्र पितरस् \\ इति ॥
5.9.m: At the north-eastern [corner], he wipes his hands: "Here, O Fathers!"

5.9.s: yajñopavītinaḥ sarve niṣkramyodañcas \\ akṣann amīmadanta \\ ity āhavanīyam upatiṣṭhante dvābhyām //
5.9.d: यज्ञोपवीतिनः सर्वे निष्क्रम्योदञ्चस् \\ अक्षन्न् अमीमदन्त \\ इत्य् आहवनीयम् उपतिष्ठन्ते द्वाभ्याम् ॥
5.9.m: All wearing the sacred thread over the left shoulder, stepping out facing north, attend upon the Āhavanīya fire with two [verses]: "They have eaten, they have rejoiced."

5.9.s: mano nv āhvāmahe \\ iti gārhapatyaṃ tisṛbhiḥ //
5.9.d: मनो न्व् आह्वामहे \\ इति गार्हपत्यं तिसृभिः ॥
5.9.m: With three [verses]: "We call upon the mind now," [they attend upon] the Gārhapatya fire.

5.9.s: prācīnāvītī praviśya \\ amīmadanta \\ iti dātā japati //
5.9.d: प्राचीनावीती प्रविश्य \\ अमीमदन्त \\ इति दाता जपति ॥
5.9.m: Wearing the sacred thread over the right shoulder, having entered, the giver mutters: "They have rejoiced."

5.9.s: avanejya pūrvavat pradakṣiṇaṃ nīviṃ visram̐sya namo vas \\ ity añjaliṃ karoti //
5.9.d: अवनेज्य पूर्ववत् प्रदक्षिणं नीविं विस्रम्̐स्य नमो वस् \\ इत्य् अञ्जलिं करोति ॥
5.9.m: Having poured water for washing as previously, clockwise, loosening the waistband, he makes a hollowed-hands gesture: "Homage to you!"

5.9.s: gṛhān naḥ pitaro datta \\ iti ca //
5.9.d: गृहान् नः पितरो दत्त \\ इति च ॥
5.9.m: and: "O Fathers, give us homes!"

5.9.s: brahmāmantraṇādi prāk srugvyūhanāt prayājavad yajñopavītiviparyayaṃ kṛtvā //
5.9.d: ब्रह्मामन्त्रणादि प्राक् स्रुग्व्यूहनात् प्रयाजवद् यज्ञोपवीतिविपर्ययं कृत्वा ॥
5.9.m: Beginning with the addressing of the Brahman up to the moving apart of the ladles, [the procedure is] like the fore-offerings, having inverted the sacred thread over the left shoulder.

5.9.s: anuprahara \\ ity ukte na kiṃ canānupraharati //
5.9.d: अनुप्रहर \\ इत्य् उक्ते न किं चनानुप्रहरति ॥
5.9.m: When it is said: "Throw into the fire!", he does not throw anything into the fire.
He silently touches himself.
Having touched [them], he does not throw the enclosing sticks into the fire.
He throws the sacrificial grass and enclosing stick into the fire,

5.10.s: nirvapati raudrān ekakapālān yāvanto yajamānagṛhyā ekādhikān //
5.10.d: निर्वपति रौद्रान् एककपालान् यावन्तो यजमानगृह्या एकाधिकान् ॥
5.10.m: He parcels out [cakes] for Rudra, baked on one potsherd, as many as there are members of the sacrificer's household, plus one more,

5.10.s: pātryāṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇāgnyulmukam ādāya catuṣpathe palāśapattramadhyamena homaḥ //
5.10.d: पात्र्यां कृत्वा दक्षिणाग्न्युल्मुकम् आदाय चतुष्पथे पलाशपत्त्रमध्यमेन होमः ॥
5.10.m: Having placed [them] in a vessel, having taken a burning coal from the Dakṣiṇa fire, the offering is made at a crossroads with the middle leaf of a palāśa [cluster].
The cutting of a portion once from each, except for the extra [cake].
He scatters the extra [cake] upon a molehill: "This is yours!"

5.10.s: āgamya \\ ava rudram adīmahi \\ iti japati //
5.10.d: आगम्य \\ अव रुद्रम् अदीमहि \\ इति जपति ॥
5.10.m: Having come, he mutters: "We have propitiated Rudra."

5.10.s: agniṃ triḥ pariyanti pitṛvat savyorūn āghnānās tryambakam iti //
5.10.d: अग्निं त्रिः परियन्ति पितृवत् सव्योरून् आघ्नानास् त्र्यम्बकम् इति ॥
5.10.m: They go around the fire three times like [in the rite for] the Fathers, slapping their left thighs: "Tryambaka!"
And like [in the rite for] the gods with this very [formula], slapping their right [thighs].
And maiden girls [go around] to the north in both cases, desiring husbands or desiring good fortune.
The sacrificer tosses up the cakes for Rudra with folded hands, as far as a cow cannot reach;

5.10.s: mūtayoḥ kṛtvā veṇuyaṣṭyāṃ kupe vāsajyobhayata sthāṇuvṛkṣavam̐śavalmīkānām anyatamasminn utkṣepaṇavad āsajati \\ etat te \\ iti //
5.10.d: मूतयोः कृत्वा वेणुयष्ट्यां कुपे वासज्योभयत स्थाणुवृक्षवम्̐शवल्मीकानाम् अन्यतमस्मिन्न् उत्क्षेपणवद् आसजति \\ एतत् ते \\ इति ॥
5.10.m: Having placed them in two woven baskets, having suspended them from a bamboo pole or a post, hanging down on both sides, he hangs [them] on any one among a post, a tree, a bamboo, or an ant-hill, as if tossing: "This is yours!"
Having returned without looking back, they touch water.

5.11.m: The rules are those of the Full-Moon sacrifice, except for the sacrificial grass.
a twelve-potsherd cake for Śunā and Sīra, or for Indra Śunāsīra;
[it is] ordinary milk, on account of the Vedic text specifying fresh-milked milk.
The sacrificial gift is a plow yoked with six [oxen].
A white horse [is the sacrificial gift] for the Sūrya cake; in its absence, a cow.

5.11.s: saṃvatsarepsoḥ phālgunyuddṛṣṭe śunāsīrīyeṇeṣṭvā somena paśuneṣṭyā vā yajeta paurṇamāsyām //
5.11.d: संवत्सरेप्सोः फाल्गुन्युद्दृष्टे शुनासीरीयेणेष्ट्वा सोमेन पशुनेष्ट्या वा यजेत पौर्णमास्याम् ॥
5.11.m: For one who desires [to complete] the year, having sacrificed with the Śunāsīrīya when the Phālguna [full moon] is visible, he should sacrifice with a soma [sacrifice], an animal sacrifice, or an iṣṭi on the full moon.
On the fast-day of the Phālguna [full moon], the Śunāsīrīya [is performed].
In the [Four-Month sacrifices] accompanied by an animal, the procedure of the animal sacrifice [prevails] on account of its primacy.
On the previous day, in the Vaiśvadeva, the animal rite [begins].
Following the animal-cake, he measures out the oblations.
Because their [offerings to] Sviṣṭakṛt are numerous.
Shaving takes place at the conclusion of the heart-spit [rite].
In the Varuṇapraghāsa rites, [an animal] for Varuṇa [is offered].
Or [it is performed] before each seasonal sacrifice.

5.12.m: The Mitravindā [iṣṭi] has ten oblations for one who desires prosperity, realm, allies, and long life.
[A cake] on eleven potsherds belongs to Indra.
[A cake] on twelve potsherds or eight potsherds belongs to Savitṛ.
[A cake] on ten potsherds belongs to Tvaṣṭṛ. There is a single offering.
The subsequent insertions of deities [may be made] as desired, because the formula of enjoyment is not heard [in the Veda].
Or in the prescribed order, because of the subordinate status of the injunction.

5.12.s: puṣṭimantāv ājyabhāgau \\ agninā rayim aśnavat \ poṣam eva divedive \ yaśasaṃ vīravattamam \ gayasphāno amīvahā \ vasuvit puṣṭivardhanaḥ \ sumitraḥ soma no bhava \\ iti //
5.12.d: पुष्टिमन्ताव् आज्यभागौ \\ अग्निना रयिम् अश्नवत् \ पोषम् एव दिवेदिवे \ यशसं वीरवत्तमम् \ गयस्फानो अमीवहा \ वसुवित् पुष्टिवर्धनः \ सुमित्रः सोम नो भव \\ इति ॥
5.12.m: The two portions of clarified butter are prosperity-granting: "Through Agni may he attain wealth, increase day by day, glorious and most rich in heroes," and "Increasing our household, slayer of disease, finder of wealth, enhancer of nourishment, be a good friend to us, Soma!"

5.12.s: haviṣo 'nuvākyā \\ agniḥ somo varuṇo mitra indras \\ bṛhaspatiḥ savitā yaḥ sahasrī \ pūṣā no gobhir avasā sarasvatī \ tvaṣṭā rūpāṇi samanktu yajñair iti //
5.12.d: हविषो ऽनुवाक्या \\ अग्निः सोमो वरुणो मित्र इन्द्रस् \\ बृहस्पतिः सविता यः सहस्री \ पूषा नो गोभिर् अवसा सरस्वती \ त्वष्टा रूपाणि समन्क्तु यज्ञैर् इति ॥
5.12.m: The invitatory verse for the oblation is: "May Agni, Soma, Varuṇa, Mitra, Indra, / Bṛhaspati, [and] thousandfold Savitṛ, / Pūṣan and Sarasvatī with cattle [and] assistance, / and Tvaṣṭṛ anoint the forms with sacrifices."

5.12.s: yājyā tvaṣṭā rūpāṇi dadatī sarasvatī \ pūṣā bhagam̐ savitā me dadātu \ bṛhaspatir dadad indro balaṃ me \ mitraḥ kṣatraṃ varuṇaḥ somo agnir iti //
5.12.d: याज्या त्वष्टा रूपाणि ददती सरस्वती \ पूषा भगम्̐ सविता मे ददातु \ बृहस्पतिर् ददद् इन्द्रो बलं मे \ मित्रः क्षत्रं वरुणः सोमो अग्निर् इति ॥
5.12.m: The offering verse is: "May Tvaṣṭṛ bestowing forms, Sarasvatī, / and Pūṣan grant me fortune, [and] Savitṛ; / may Bṛhaspati grant me vigor, and Indra, / Mitra royal power, Varuṇa, Soma, [and] Agni."

5.13.s: tvaṣṭā rūpāṇām̐ rūpakṛd rūpapatī rūpeṇa paśūn asmin yajñe mayi dadhātu svāhā \\ iti //
5.13.d: त्वष्टा रूपाणाम्̐ रूपकृद् रूपपती रूपेण पशून् अस्मिन् यज्ञे मयि दधातु स्वाहा \\ इति ॥
5.13.m: [He offers with the mantra]: "May Tvaṣṭṛ, maker of forms of forms, lord of forms, place cattle in me with form at this sacrifice, svāhā!"

5.13.s: sahasravatyau vā nū no rāsva sahasravat \ tokavat puṣṭimad vasu \ dyumad agne suvīryam \\ varṣiṣṭham anupakṣitam \ uta no brahmann aviṣas \\ uktheṣu devahūtamaḥ \ śaṃ naḥ śocā marudvṛdhas \\ agne sahasrasātamas \\ iti //
5.13.d: सहस्रवत्यौ वा नू नो रास्व सहस्रवत् \ तोकवत् पुष्टिमद् वसु \ द्युमद् अग्ने सुवीर्यम् \\ वर्षिष्ठम् अनुपक्षितम् \ उत नो ब्रह्मन्न् अविषस् \\ उक्थेषु देवहूतमः \ शं नः शोचा मरुद्वृधस् \\ अग्ने सहस्रसातमस् \\ इति ॥
5.13.m: Or [they are] two verses containing the word 'thousand': "Now grant us thousandfold wealth, possessing offspring and nourishment, luminous, Agni, with good heroes, supreme and undecaying," and "And, O priest, may you aid us in hymns, most devoted to invocations of the gods; shine prosperity upon us, increaser of the Maruts, O Agni, best winner of thousands!"

6.1.m: The animal sacrifice [is performed] every year in the rainy season.

6.1.s: yūpāhutiṃ juhoti caturgṛhītam̐ sruveṇa vā \\ uru viṣṇo \\ iti //
6.1.d: यूपाहुतिं जुहोति चतुर्गृहीतम्̐ स्रुवेण वा \\ उरु विष्णो \\ इति ॥
6.1.m: He offers the sacrificial-post oblation with four ladlings [of butter], or with the dipping spoon, with the formula: "O wide-striding Viṣṇu!"
Taking the remainder of the clarified butter, he goes accompanied by the carpenter.
He touches the sacrificial post [to be cut] with the mantra: "Surpassing others..."
Or, standing facing east, he addresses it with the mantra.

6.1.s: pālāśaṃ bahulaparṇam aśuṣkāgram ūrdhvaśakalaśākhaṃ madhyāgropanatam abraṇam //
6.1.d: पालाशं बहुलपर्णम् अशुष्काग्रम् ऊर्ध्वशकलशाखं मध्याग्रोपनतम् अब्रणम् ॥
6.1.m: [The post should be] of palāśa wood, abundant in leaves, with an un-withered tip, with branches rising upwards, bent toward the middle and tip, and without defects.
In its absence, [one should use] khadira, bilva, or rohitaka trees.
In the soma sacrifice, in the absence of khadira, [he uses] the others.
He touches it with the dipping spoon with the formula: "For Viṣṇu, thee!"

6.1.s: oṣadhe \\ iti kuśataruṇaṃ tiraskṛtya svadhite \\ iti paraśunā praharati //
6.1.d: ओषधे \\ इति कुशतरुणं तिरस्कृत्य स्वधिते \\ इति परशुना प्रहरति ॥
6.1.m: Interposing a shoot of kuśa grass with [the mantra], "O plant," he strikes with the axe with [the mantra], "O axe!"
He preserves the first chip [of wood].
He cuts [the tree] so that it does not stay fixed at the axle height.

6.1.s: dyāṃ mā lekhīr iti patantam abhimantrayate //
6.1.d: द्यां मा लेखीर् इति पतन्तम् अभिमन्त्रयते ॥
6.1.m: As it falls, he addresses it with [the formula], "Do not scrape the sky!"
"For this [axe cuts] you" is [for] smoothing [the tree].
Or it is the remainder of the address, because the instruction is without distinction.
He offers an oblation on the stump with [the mantra], "From this [stump], you..."
After trimming around, [there is] a further cutting.
Some [teachers prescribe lengths] starting from one cubit.
He makes it eight-cornered, except for the unworked lower part (upara).
From the top [part], he makes the head-ring (caṣāla), span-long, eight-cornered, and constricted in the middle.
He fixes it over the top [of the post].
The top of the sacrificial post projects two or three finger-breadths beyond the opening [of the caṣāla].
In the Soma [sacrifice], it is five cubits long up to fifteen [cubits], excluding ten, seven, and fourteen;
twenty-one in the Aśvamedha.

6.1.s: vediṃ kariṣyan ṣaḍḍhotāraṃ pañcagṛhītaṃ manasānudrutya juhoty ekām āhutiṃ pañca vā dyauṣ pṛṣṭham antarikṣam ātmāṅgair yajñaṃ pṛthivīm̐ śarīrair \ vācaspate 'chidrayā vācāchidrayā juhvā divi devāvṛdham̐ hotrām airayant svāhā \\ iti
6.1.d: वेदिं करिष्यन् षड्ढोतारं पञ्चगृहीतं मनसानुद्रुत्य जुहोत्य् एकाम् आहुतिं पञ्च वा द्यौष् पृष्ठम् अन्तरिक्षम् आत्माङ्गैर् यज्ञं पृथिवीम्̐ शरीरैर् \ वाचस्पते ऽछिद्रया वाचाछिद्रया जुह्वा दिवि देवावृधम्̐ होत्राम् ऐरयन्त् स्वाहा \\ इति
6.1.m: Intending to make the altar (vedi), he murmurs mentally the six-hotṛ formula with five ladlefuls and offers one oblation or five, with: "Sky is the back, atmosphere the self, sacrifice with limbs, earth with bodies; O lord of speech, with unfailing speech, with unfailing ladle, they raised the Hotṛ's offering in heaven, increasing the gods; svāhā!"

6.2.m: He makes the altar as in the Varuṇapraghāsa.
He brings forward one [fire] together with the fuel bundle.

He should perform the taking up of the vow, the carrying forward of the praṇītā waters, the portions of clarified butter, the cutting of portions, the full cup, and the steps of Viṣṇu, because of the rule for animal and grain sacrifices.

Having performed the strewing of grass, the setting out of utensils, sprinkling, pouring out of clarified butter, and putting it on the fire, he performs the rites beginning with the northern boundary-trace up to the setting down of clarified butter.
The taking of the clarified butter is with spotted butter (pṛṣadājya).
He strews branches of the plakṣa tree on the sacrificial grass.

6.2.s: devasya tvā \\ ity abhrim ādāya yūpāvaṭaṃ parilikhati \\ idam aham ity āhavanīyasya purastād antarvedyardham //
6.2.d: देवस्य त्वा \\ इत्य् अभ्रिम् आदाय यूपावटं परिलिखति \\ इदम् अहम् इत्य् आहवनीयस्य पुरस्ताद् अन्तर्वेद्यर्धम् ॥
6.2.m: Taking the shovel with [the mantra], "At the impulse of the divine [Savitṛ]...", he traces the hole for the post with "Here I [cast away the spell]..." in front of the Āhavanīya fire, half inside the altar.
He digs [it] equal to the lower part (upara).
He throws out the loose earth toward the east.
Before it, he lays down the sacrificial post pointing eastward.
A handful of kuśa grass upon it;
and to the north of the top, the head-ring (caṣāla).

6.2.s: yavo 'si \\ ity apsu yavān opya prokṣaty agramadhyamūlāni dive tvā \\ iti pratimantram //
6.2.d: यवो ऽसि \\ इत्य् अप्सु यवान् ओप्य प्रोक्षत्य् अग्रमध्यमूलानि दिवे त्वा \\ इति प्रतिमन्त्रम् ॥
6.2.m: Having thrown barley grains into water with "You are barley," he sprinkles the top, middle, and base [of the post], each with its respective mantra beginning with: "For the sky, you!"
[The word] "I sprinkle" is added everywhere, because of syntactic requirement.
He pours the remainder [of the water] into the hole with "Let [the divine waters] be cleansed!"

6.2.s: barhīm̐ṣi prāñcy udañci ca prāsyati pitṛṣadanam asi \\ iti //
6.2.d: बर्हीम्̐षि प्राञ्च्य् उदञ्चि च प्रास्यति पितृषदनम् असि \\ इति ॥
6.2.m: He throws sacrificial grass pointing east and north [into the hole] with: "You are the seat of the ancestors."
And the first chip with: "You are the leader."
He silently makes an oblation into the hole with the dipping spoon.

6.2.s: purastāt parikramyādhvaryur yajamāno vā yūpam anakty udaṅṅ upaviśya //
6.2.d: पुरस्तात् परिक्रम्याध्वर्युर् यजमानो वा यूपम् अनक्त्य् उदङ्ङ् उपविश्य ॥
6.2.m: Going around from the front, the Adhvaryu or the sacrificer, sitting facing north, anoints the sacrificial post.
